articleTitle: Development of sub-millimeter high power compact EIKs for DNP and radar applications
abstract: This paper presents recently performed at CPI Canada development of high power 263 GHz CW EIO generator for DNP enhancement and pulsed 263 GHz EIK for radar applications.

articleTitle: New slow wave structure for W-band TWT
abstract: A new slow wave structure based on CVD diamond substrate for W-band TWT is considered. Dispersion properties, thermal characteristics, gain, output power are calculated. Coupling to output waveguides is simulated. Fabrication problems are investigated.

articleTitle: Fabrication of W-band TWT for 5G small cells backhaul
abstract: The W-band (92-95 GHz) Traveling Wave Tube enabling the first Point to multipoint millimeter wave backhaul wireless network is in final phase of fabrication. The challenge is to build a TWT suitable for large volume fabrication to satisfy the cost constraints of network operators. Performances are targeted to provide coverage on sectors up to 90° with 1 km range. Simulations demonstrate a bandwidth of operation in excess of 5 GHz with a saturated output power of 40 W. The TWT is directly connected to a sector horn antenna.

articleTitle: The PCM focused millimeter-wave sheet beam TWT
abstract: The research and development of period cusp magnet (PCM) focused millimeter-wave sheet beam traveling wave tubes based on the double staggered grating waveguide are presented both in Ku and Q band. In the hot test, the Ku band tube provides a beam transmission of 81% and more than 15kW peak output power, while the Q band design provides a beam transmission about 92% and more than 1.4kW peak output power. Specifications including the gun, PCM, RF and hot test are discussed.

articleTitle: An overview of European spaceborne vacuum tube amplifiers and system needs
abstract: The paper aims at providing an overview of European vacuum tube amplifiers used for space-borne applications in the field of Telecommunications and Earth Observation. The overview also describes current system needs in the different domains and discusses development plans at the European Space Agency.

articleTitle: MAGIC2-D simulations of high efficiency klystrons using the core oscillation method
abstract: Klystrons employing traditional monotonic electron bunching are capable of efficiencies up to ~70%. The use of the core oscillation method (COM) of electron bunching has predicted a significant improvement in efficiency towards 90%. Here, we document refinements on previously presented geometries, with PIC simulations predicting efficiencies up to 85%.

articleTitle: Planar V-band slow-wave structures for low-voltage tubes with sheet electron beam
abstract: Planar slow-wave structures (SWS) on dielectric substrates at V-band (50-70 GHz) are studied. The SWS circuits are designed and fabricated. Basic electromagnetic parameters of the SWS are calculated. We consider the meander and interdigital SWSs, which are designed for operation in O-type traveling-wave tube amplifier and backward-wave oscillator, respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation of a rectangular waveguide with a magnetic wall made of mushroom-shaped metamaterial
abstract: The paper presents the results of computer simulation of electromagnetic wave propagation in a standard rectangular waveguide R32 type with the cross-section 72,14×34,04 mm, one of the wide walls of which are made in the form of the mushroom-shaped metamaterial magnetic wall. Using the electromagnetic simulation methods the dependences of the field distribution during simulation of the fundamental mode H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>, the characteristics of the complex reflection coefficient S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> on the frequency and the near field radiation pattern of the waveguide are obtained.

articleTitle: Particle-in-cell simulation of second and third harmonic cavity klystron
abstract: This paper outlines the results obtained from Magic software for the CSM_23 (Core Stabilization Method) klystron. This klystron implements the use of a second and third harmonic klystron to increase the efficiency. From the PIC simulation an efficiency of 78.1% was achieved.

articleTitle: Virtual cathode oscillator with elliptical resonator
abstract: We have proposed the new scheme of relativistic vircator system for generation of high-power microwave radiation with elliptical resonator as the interaction space and have carried out its numerical study. The effect of the resonator parameters on the interaction of electron beam with the electrodynamic structure has been discovered. We have conducted optimization of the power output of the system. We the possibility to achieve efficiency up to 5% in such virtual cathode generator that is essential for vircators.

articleTitle: High precision frequency stabilization of a 100W/263 GHz continuous wave gyrotron
abstract: The width of the frequency spectrum as narrow as 1 Hz has been obtained at the output radiation of a THz band continuous wave gyrotron at the power level about 100 Watts. The phase lock loop control of anode voltage has been used. The long-term stability was defined by reference clock.

articleTitle: Development of a high-efficiency klystron based on the kladistron principle
abstract: We are developing a high-efficiency klystron to perform particle accelerators cavities conditioning. We first verify this concept with an enhanced version of the Thales TH2166 klystron. After we designed the new interaction line, we focused on the development of the cavities' tuning system and the study of the multipactor phenomenon.

articleTitle: Numerical studies on the influence of cavity thermal expansion on the performance of a high-power gyrotron
abstract: An iterative procedure is described, which models the influence of the thermal expansion of the gyrotron cavity on the expected gyrotron performance. It is a multi-physics simulation method, which involves electrodynamic, thermohydraulic, and thermo-mechanical simulations. The method is applied to the first European 170 GHz, 1 MW CW prototype gyrotron for ITER. According to calculations, a performance reduction of ~15% is expected at nominal operating parameters because of the simulated thermal expansion of the cavity. An alternative operating point to mitigate this effect is proposed.

articleTitle: L3 technologies EDD Q/V-band helix TWT for future high-data-rate communications uplink applications
abstract: For next generation high-data-rate satellite communication systems, L3 Technologies, Electron Devices Division (EDD) has successfully developed an uplink Q/V-band helix TWT, the 8936H, that can produce 250-W saturated peak output power with overall efficiency up to 46% across 47.0 to 52.4-GHz bandwidth. The 8936H can operate up to 150-W CW over 47.0 to 51.4 GHz (low band) and up to 125-W CW over 51.4 to 52.4 GHz (high band) with full thermal stability.

articleTitle: Novel multistage depressed collector for high power fusion gyrotrons based on an E×B drift concept
abstract: A novel concept of a two-stage depressed collector for high-power, fusion gyrotrons using helix electrodes is investigated. The helix electrodes create an azimuthal component of the electric field, which causes a radial drift of the annular electron beam. This drift sorts the electrons according to their initial velocities. Particle-in-Cell simulations show that this concept is extremely robust against the negative effect of secondary electrons. The collector efficiency is reduced by only 1 %. Considering the space charge (including that of secondary electrons) a collector efficiency of 77 % can be achieved with only two stages. Furthermore, electron beam sweeping may be possible at the last stage, where the most kinetic energy of electrons is absorbed.

articleTitle: Comparison of 6 MW S-band pulsed BAC MBK with the existing SBKs
abstract: S-band BAC MBK BT258 was developed at VDBT with support of CERN. Two samples of MBK were fabricated and tested at VDBT. Maximum efficiency of 64,5% was obtained at an output level of 6,4 MW. The efficiency in the vicinity of 60% for one of MBKs was successively confirmed in tests at CERN. Comparison of output parameters of MBK with the existing classical klystrons is given in the article.

articleTitle: Electron-wave momentum exchange and time domain simulations applied to traveling wave tubes
abstract: We presented at the 2013 and 2015 IVEC conferences a new discrete model for the traveling wave tube (TWT) as an alternative to PIC and frequency algorithms. Since then, we upgraded the model to consider hamiltonian aspects of the dynamics (better ensuring physical conservation laws). We also provide a new formulation for the electromagnetic momentum and power in tubes, offering further opportunities to characterize wave-electrons interactions.

articleTitle: UV-LIGA microfabrication of 0.3 THz double corrugated waveguide
abstract: A microfabrication process has been developed by using ultraviolet photolithography (UV-LIGA) with multi-layer SU-8 photoresist to create high aspect ratio Slow Wave Structures (SWS) for millimeter waves and THz vacuum electron devices. The main steps of the process will be described, applied to the fabrication of a double corrugated waveguide at 300 GHz..

articleTitle: A fast optimized algorithm based on the NSGA — II for microwave windows
abstract: Based on the Mode-Matching Technique (MMT), a fast optimized method based on NSGA-II (Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm) algorithm is proposed for design of waveguide windows. Unlike the conventional micro-genetic algorithm, we construct two different objective functions as optimal goals of NSGA-II and the values of the objective functions are evaluated fast and accurately by MMT. For a waveguide window of W-Band folded waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube, the optimized results have shown excellent transmission performance from 83GHz to 103GHz with S11 less than -25dB, which is yielded with population size of 25 in less than fifteen iterations.

articleTitle: A multistage depressed collector system for gyrotrons
abstract: Enhancement of overall efficiency of gyrotrons can be achieved by recovery of electron energy using multistage depressed collector systems. For such systems, a new method of spatial separation of electrons with different energies was proposed. It is based on application of azimuthal magnetic field which, in combination with axial electric field, causes a radial drift of electrons. In this paper, the main features of this method are described and design of the 4-stage depressed collector system for the SPbPU's experimental 74.2 GHz, 100 kW gyrotron are presented.

articleTitle: First CW experiments with the EU ITER 1 MW, 170 GHz industrial prototype gyrotron
abstract: The EU 1 MW, 170 GHz gyrotron for ECH&CD on ITER has been developed by EGYC (European GYrotron Consortium) under the coordination of Fusion for Energy (F4E) and in cooperation with the industrial partner Thales Electron Devices (TED). The manufacturing of the first industrial continuous-wave (CW) prototype gyrotron, has been completed in November 2015 at TED. The tube was delivered to KIT and the experimental verification started in February 2016 in the short-pulse (SP) regime. Since October 2016 the gyrotron is in CW operation. In this work, details regarding the experiments at the KIT test-stand with pulses up to 180 s are presented.

articleTitle: A truncated sine waveguide for G-band TWT
abstract: A truncated sine waveguide slow wave structure (SWS) is proposed for the wideband high-power terahertz traveling-wave tube (TWT). The slow-wave characteristics including the dispersion properties and interaction impedances have been investigated by the simulation method. Compared to the sine waveguide, the average interaction impedance of the truncated sine waveguide is increased by 31.1% at 0.22THz. Meanwhile, the transmission properties of the truncated sine waveguide SWS is as excellent as the sine waveguide from the calculations.

articleTitle: A compact G-band MPM power amplifier for high-resolution airborne radar
abstract: A compact, upper-mm-wave, microwave power module (MPM) power amplifier operating in G-band from 231.5 GHz to 235 GHz has been developed at L3 Electron Devices. Two MPM configurations have been tested: The first, intended for laboratory use, consists of a single-housing containing a PPM-focused serpentine waveguide traveling wave tube and a compact 20 kV high voltage power supply. This MPM provides a peak output power of 41 dBm at 234 GHz when driven with 7 dBm input. The second MPM is configured for use in a modified tactical airborne gimbal. It employs a custom split-package architecture consisting of separate power supply and RF modules, along with interconnecting cabling. This unit has been qualified for airborne operation up to 20 kft (6 km) and provides greater than 44 dBm at 234 GHz when driven with 11 dBm input drive. Both MPMs operate from 270 VDC prime power and at duty factors up to 50%. Radar waveforms have been processed through both amplifiers. We believe this development represents the first realization of an integrated G-band MPM.

articleTitle: W-band helical-waveguide gyro-TWTs yielding high gain and high output power: Design and simulations
abstract: A cascade of two gyrotron travelling-wave tubes (gyro-TWTs), one of those possesses a relatively high gain (46 dB) while the other provides high output power (350 kW) at the moderate (22 dB) gain, is under design and modeling. Both gyro-TWTs use helically corrugated waveguides and operate at the second cyclotron harmonic. A principal scheme of such an amplifier chain is discussed including issues of microwave input, output and transmission between the tubes. Computer modeling of the beam-wave interaction using CST Particle Studio PIC Solver shows feasibility of achieving of 350 kW pulse output power with 6-8 GHz bandwidth when driving by a 50-mW input source at W-band.

articleTitle: Additive vacuum electronics: Electron beam melting of copper
abstract: The construction of vacuum electronic devices is an artisan process; it requires extremes of high precision machining and assembly and the tolerances and feature sizes become more exacting as the frequency increases. Merging of copper additive manufacturing and electropolishing technologies will produce low-cost, high-throughput fabrication techniques for construction of fully integrated vacuum electronic devices. Technology demonstrations at two frequencies (S-Band and W-band) will address the demand for fast turnaround manufacturing of travelling wave tube amplifiers in legacy military systems as well as in the emerging high frequency applications.

articleTitle: 170-W radiation-cooled, space K-band TWT
abstract: L3 Technologies Electron Devices Division (L3 EDD) has completed space-flight qualification thermal vacuum testing for a 170-W radiation-cooled K band TWT. Performance data and thermal analysis from the testing will be discussed.

articleTitle: A microfabricated V-shaped microstrip meander-line slow-wave structure
abstract: A novel configuration for a Ka-band V-shaped microstrip meander-line slow-wave structure (SWS) is reported. All the components of the proposed configuration can be realized using standard microfabrication processes. CPW input/output feed-lines, which can be fabricated together with the SWS, are incorporated in order to permit on-wafer measurement of cold-test parameters. Simulated dispersion characteristics and coupling impedance for a wideband design are presented. The results show that the S11 of the entire structure is better than -20 dB over a 25% bandwidth centered at 30 GHz. The steps for microfabrication of the SWS are also described briefly.

articleTitle: Development of a C-band high power amplifier Klystron for linear electron accelerators
abstract: JSC Research and Production Corporation “Toriy” has designed and manufactured the KIU-271, a high peak power, high gain, C-band klystron. The klystron operates at 5712 MHz, with 3.0 MW peak output power, 25kW average output power, and gain of 50 dB. Experimental date is presented.

articleTitle: High emission current density electron gun for a 263 GHz sheet beam traveling wave tube
abstract: The design and testing of an electron gun for a 263 GHz sheet beam traveling wave tube is described. An elliptical cathode emits a 0.1518 A electron beam with 40 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> loading. The emitted beam is compressed to a high current density (460 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) beam with a highly elongated elliptical cross section of 0.60 × 0.07 mm by a special shaped electrode and an extruded anode. The test data show that the electron gun can provide sufficient current for the device, and the high beam transmission promises a successful device performance.

articleTitle: A simple pillbox-type mixed-mode window for high power microwave devices
abstract: Simulation results of a simple and compact pillboxtype window having reduced RF electric field at the periphery of the ceramic disk are described in the paper. The window uses mixed traveling TE11 and evanescent TM11 modes and is designed for a 5.712 GHz (10 kW average and 3 MW peak output power) klystron.

articleTitle: Development of a 0.32 THz folded waveguide TWT
abstract: A traveling wave tube vacuum electronic (VE) amplifier operating above 300 GHz has being developed. This VE amplifier is based on a folded waveguide slow-wave circuit, together with a periodic permanent magnet system. The amplifier achieved 19.6 dB of gain, and 134mW of maximum output power.

articleTitle: Development of millimeter-wave space TWTs in BVERI
abstract: This paper describes the design, performance test, qualification test, lifetime experiment of millimeter wave space traveling wave tubes in Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Institute (BVERI). There has been series products of 20W, 30W, 55W and 100W with 55-60% overall efficiency and good linearity at Ka-band, and 45/60W power at Q-band and 30W power at V bands with 35-45% efficiency. Now there are 14 tubes in-orbit with stable operation and a single longest time of 12,000Hrs.

articleTitle: Study of multiple beam backward wave oscillator based on corrugated waveguide TWT
abstract: The multiple beam Backward Wave Oscillator (BWO) which based on corrugated waveguide is simulated by Microwave Tube Simulation Suite (MTSS) and CST Particle Studio(PIC). Simulation results show that the saturated output power is about 45W at the expected operating frequency of 220GHz, when the cylindrical electron beam current and Voltage are 20 mA and 44keV.

articleTitle: Mechanical analysis of Ku band radiation cooled space travelling wave tube
abstract: Vibration and Shock from the rocket launch bring high demands for the design of radiation cooled space travelling wave tube. In the paper, dynamic analysis of Ku band radiation cooled space travelling wave tube was carried on by means of finite element analysis method according to environmental conditions. And an optimized prototype was made and tested.

articleTitle: MEMS fabrication of H-plane and E-plane loaded 400 GHz TWT amplifier
abstract: In this paper, we report UV-LIGA technique employed to fabricate a newly proposed H-plane and E-plane loaded metallic slow-wave structure for THz TWT amplifier. A negative tone photoresist KMPR is used as the mold material in the process. The fabrication process includes lithography, electroplating, mold removal and polishing. The process parameters were optimized according to the designed structure features. For the fabricated structure, the dimensional accuracy was within 2.5 μm and the RMS sidewall surface roughness was less than 75 nm.

articleTitle: Mode analysis of an overmoded extended interaction cavity in terahertz EIK
abstract: The extended interaction klystron (EIK) operating at high order mode has many advantages compared with conventional EIK in high frequency band for its oversized structure. A five-gap cavity operating at the TM31-2π mode with resonant frequency of 0.34 THz is investigated in this paper. Resonant modes in the overmoded cavity are analyzed for mode selection and stable operation. Finally, the cavity is theoretically approved stable operation at the TM31-2π mode without self-oscillation and mode competition under 15 kV beam voltage and 300 mA beam current.

articleTitle: Manufacturing and performance results of a 1.2 MW peak, 704 MHz multi-beam inductive output tube
abstract: A multi-beam inductive output tube (MB-IOT) is being developed that will produce over 1.2 MW peak power at 704 MHz with over 65% efficiency. This is a collaborative effort between Thales Electron Devices (TED) and Communications & Power Industries (CPI) to design and fabricate a new RF source for the European Spallation Source (ESS). Main design features and measured performances will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of a 5.8 GHz power-variable phase-controlled magnetron
abstract: In this study, we developed a 5.8 GHz power-variable phase-controlled magnetron (PVPCM), which utilizes an injection locking method and phase locked loop (PLL) method. We had developed a PVPCM for a 2.45 GHz oven magnetron and we applied the same method to the 5.8 GHz magnetron. In this method, we control the phase of 5.8 GHz magnetron output by a phase shifter without the anode current control PLL method. Then we can control the output power of the magnetron by controlling the anode current. Our experiments show that, the developed PVPCM had a 655 W stable output power, the phase locked response time was less than 50 μs, and the phase-locked stability was lower than ±5°.

articleTitle: Asymptotic boundary conditions for the finite element modeling of axisymmetric period permanent magnet structures
abstract: In this paper, asymptotic boundary conditions with finite element method for axisymmetric permanent magnet focusing system is presented. Asymptotic boundary conditions is implemented in magnetic field simulator (MFS). And the asymptotic boundary conditions has been applied to improve calculating precision and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Simplified tape-helix analysis of planar helix slow-wave structure using effective dielectric constant method
abstract: Tape-helix analysis is presented for dispersion characteristics of a planar helix slow-wave structure with straight-edge connections. The analysis is simplified in a novel way by using the effective dielectric constant method, which avoids the application of boundary conditions for side connections. The results obtained from analysis show a good match with simulation results. The simplified analysis also provides more accurate results than the previously reported results for the rectangular helix based on tape-helix analysis.

articleTitle: Efficient relativistic magnetron with lengthy virtual cathode formed using the magnetic mirror effect
abstract: In this paper we describe a relativistic magnetron with diffraction output (MDO) that uses a lengthy virtual cathode (VC) instead of a physical cathode as the source of electrons. Unlike our earlier work where the lengthy VC was formed from two VCs that were generated at the input and output of the MDO, here we describe using the magnetic mirror effect instead of the VC at the output of the MDO to not only form a lengthy VC, but also to eliminate axial leakage current to achieve even higher efficiency operation.

articleTitle: Investigation on misalignment tolerances of 240-GHz DEMO gyrotrons
abstract: Considering the design goals and technological constraints for DEMO gyrotrons, conceptual design and tolerance analyses of a 236 GHz 1 MW conventional, hollow-cavity gyrotron and of a 237.5 GHz 2 MW coaxial-cavity gyrotron are ongoing at KIT. At such high power and frequency, very high order operating modes (eigenvalues > 100) are necessary to keep cavity wall loading at 2 kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Both the small wavelength and the high eigenvalue make the gyrotrons susceptible to misalignment of electron beam and - if present - coaxial insert. For the hollow-cavity gyrotron, the influence of the off-axis electron beam on gyrotron operation has been very accurately investigated in interaction simulations with realistic beam parameters. For the coaxial-cavity gyrotron, the influence of insert misalignment on modes and on an aligned electron beam has been studied.

articleTitle: Research progress of a W-band 100-Watts extended interaction oscillator
abstract: This paper introduces the research progress of a W-band Extended Interaction Oscillator (EIO). The EIO is designed to produce a continuous wave power of over 100 Watts at nearby 95GHz operating frequency, whose operating voltage is 11 kV with a beam current of 0.15 A. Refer to components of the EIO, the electron optics system is designed as a typical Pierce type with permanent magnet structure, and simulation results indicate that the gun has a reasonable cathode loading and a beam-to-tunnel radial fill factor of less than 0.625, and the peak value of longitudinal magnetic field in the interaction region is ∼7200Guass. And, the RF system design adopts trapezoidal slow wave structure with dual coupling slots and 24 periods, and the beam-wave interaction of RF system is simulated by CST software and PIC (Particle in Cell) code separately. Meanwhile, the test results of group delay for RF system are compared with the calculation, and the comparison results are basically the same, which meets the design requirement.

articleTitle: Development of new generation of cathodes using additive manufacturing methods
abstract: Fast warm-up cathodes are used in multiple, mostly military applications where rapid turn-on is required. These cathodes are designed to reach operating temperature in less than five seconds, with high reliability. High reliability is critical since eventual end use of this product is only one mission. To achieve these requirements, fast warm-up cathodes have to be made with low thermal mass, high thermal efficiency, and strong mechanical integrity and uniform temperature profile. Current technology provides cathodes capable of reaching the operating temperature in 3-4 seconds, using a very thin pressed and sintered tungsten emitter, a 2D (pancake) tungsten-rhenium wire heater, and low mass support structure with thin re-entry sleeves for predictable thermal expansion. Ceradyne, a 3M Company, is developing a new technology, using 3D printed emitter and multilayer ceramic heater, which is expected to reduce the warm-up time by another 1-1.5 second.

articleTitle: Super-high power gyrotrons for electron-cyclotron plasma heating
abstract: Design peculiarities and operational parameters of modern Russian gyrotrons developed for 105-170 GHz frequency range with pulse duration up to 3600 s and output power of 1-1.5MW at efficiency over 50 % (CPD collector) are presented.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of electron gun using finite element method
abstract: The electron gun plays a significant role in determining the life and reliability of TWTs which are core components of the modern communication devices, radar, medical systems and scientific research areas. Using the finite element method, a software package Thermal Simulator (TS) which can be used for thermal analysis of Electron Gun was developed. To validate TS, numerical results for a simplified electron gun are shown compared with ANSYS.

articleTitle: Long pulse operation of a high power microwave source with a metamaterial loaded waveguide
abstract: We present the design and the experimental results of a metamaterial (MTM) based backward wave oscillator (BWO). The electron beam propagates through a waveguide loaded with two MTM plates, with the design of one plate being the reverse of the second plate. The design mode is a fundamental hybrid deflecting mode at 2.4 GHz with a negative group velocity. CST PIC simulations predict megawatt level output power with a helical beam trajectory, indicating the Cherenkov-cyclotron type interaction. In the experiment, microsecond long microwave pulses at a power level of up to 2.9 MW were generated by an electron beam with a beam voltage of up to 490 kV and current of 84 A.

articleTitle: TWT output signal denoising based on improved wavelet threshold
abstract: Based on hard, soft and semi-soft threshold method, an improved threshold method for TWT output signal is proposed. The mathematical model of wavelet threshold denoising for TWT output signal is established. The experimental signal of TWT is denoised using wavelet threshold method. The results show that SNR increased from 44.55dB to 50.15dB, and the improved wavelet threshold method is better than hard, soft and semi-soft threshold method for the output signal of TWT.

articleTitle: Novel geometries for magnetic circuit optimization
abstract: The performance of vacuum devices often rely on having a uniform magnetic field in the interaction region of the device. Here the EM solver from CST Microwave Studio (MWS) is used to optimize the pole-piece and magnet shape for a magnetic circuit to make use of the maximum energy product (BHmax) and improve its' efficiency (BH/BHmax). For a desired field increase it can be shown that the simple cylindrical magnet designs can be improved upon by making more efficient use of the available BHmax. Optimized geometries shown here can achieve an improved efficiency, from 65% to 85%, coupled with a field enhancement and without cost impact.

articleTitle: A re doped Y2O3-Gd2O3-HfO2 W base direct-heated cathode
abstract: In this paper we mainly describe the research progress in a kind of Re doped Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> W base direct-heated cathode, which includes the emission current and the lifetime testing of the cathode. The test results show that the DC emission is beyond 3.23A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 1500 °Cbr. The lifetime is reached 4000h with a DC load 1.5A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 1600 °Cbr. And the anti-electron-bombing characteristic of the cathode is also studied. Experimental results show that the cathode has good anti-electron-bombing capability.

articleTitle: Volterra-based modeling of traveling wave tube amplifier for system level simulation
abstract: This paper describes a Volterra-based model of frequency dependent AM-AM and AM-PM conversions of a nonlinear traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) for use in communication system level simulation. The proposed method provides a systematic way to identify the model and ensures numerical stability in coefficient extraction. Comparison between simulation results and measurements are presented in terms of gain and noise power ratio (NPR).

articleTitle: Measurements of satellite modes in 140 GHz wendelstein 7-X gyrotrons: An approach to an electronic stability control
abstract: The stellarator Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) uses electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) by 140 GHz highpower microwave sources (gyrotrons) for plasma generation and as primary heating method. At the limit of operational stability, parasitic and satellite modes simultaneously excited to the working mode are converted to stray radiation in the gyrotron, resulting in a reduced efficiency and mostly in a mode loss. Hence the stray radiation level by these modes is proposed as an indicator for the operational stability. A feedback control system ensuring stable operation of the gyrotrons at highest possible output power and a fast mode recovery after a mode loss, is desirable for the ECRH on W7-X. Consequently shot spectrograms and the signal of a RF detector were examined to identify a reliable mode-loss-precursor in the stray radiation at the gyrotron relief window for the targeted control system. This information then can be used to derive and implement a control algorithm on a field programmable gate array (FPGA).

articleTitle: Pulse-shortening in recirculating planar magnetrons
abstract: Recent experiments on the UM Recirculating Planar Magnetron (RPM) [1], have utilized a 12-frame ultra-fast intensified CCD camera to analyze the effect of anode and cathode plasma formation on microwave pulse duration. The experiments were driven by MELBA-C, a Marx-Abramyan system, which delivers a −300 kV voltage pulse for 0.3-1.0 μs, with a 0.13-0.31 T axial magnetic field applied by a pair of electromagnets. The RPM was tested with both an S-band (2 GHz) and L-band (1 GHz) anode, as well as two different cathodes with substantially different thickness and end caps. A smaller anode-cathode gap, coupled with larger end-loss current, produced brighter plasma and allowed for improvements in temporal resolution of the imaging configuration. Many shots demonstrated a direct correlation between anode-plasma formation and a sharp reduction in RF power.

articleTitle: Development and production of a 704 MHz, 1.5 MW peak power klystron
abstract: Communications & Power Industries LLC has designed and manufactured the VKP-8292A, a high peak power, high efficiency, UHF band klystron. The klystron operates at 704.42 MHz, with 1.59 MW peak output power, 78 kW average output power, and a gain of 45 dB. The klystron is designed to operate between 0.3 MW and 1.2 MW in the linear range of the transfer curve. The klystron is over 67% efficient at nominal beam voltage and includes optimization for efficiency at lower beam voltages. Experimental and predicted performance data are compared.

articleTitle: 3D-printed mold electroforming for microfabrication of W-band TWT circuits
abstract: We demonstrate a method for fabricating upper millimeter-wave TWT circuits and passive components, based on additive manufacturing and copper electroforming. The method allows the creation of a solid copper circuit, suitable for high-power vacuum electronic devices, beginning with a plastic inverse mold built on a commercial 3D printer. We present progress on W-band serpentine waveguide circuits fabricated in copper by this 3D-printed mold electroforming (3D-PriME) process.

articleTitle: Efficient calculation of impedance matrices for VE device circuit structures
abstract: This paper presents an efficient method for the calculation of impedance matrices of slow and standing wave structures used in vacuum electronic devices. These matrices can be imported by large signal parametric codes like TESLA-Z and CHRISTINE-CC for accurate small and large signal analysis of TWTs, klystrons and other VE devices [1], including effects of all geometric features and material properties included in the calculation of the impedance matrix. The technique employs both lumped (internal) and wave (modal, boundary) ports in the 3D finite element electromagnetic (EM) code ANALYST [2].

articleTitle: Initial design of electron optics system for an L-band klystron
abstract: In order to adopt the ring electron beam in an L-Band klystron with coaxial beam tunnel, the ring electron beam was divided into three sector-ring electron beams with a voltage of 120kV and a total current of 140A. In this paper, the electron gun and the focusing system were established, the emission and the transmission of the electron beam were simulated, and the simulation results show that the transmission distance of the electron beam attains to 1250mm.

articleTitle: Application of reciprocity to the design of electron guns
abstract: We develop a sensitivity function for the design of electron guns, based on a form of reciprocity implicit in Hamilton's equations of motion. The sensitivity function allows for the determination of the effect of small, arbitrary changes in electrode potentials, electrode positions, and magnet locations on specific beam quality figures of merit with a single, time-reversed run of a beam optics code. The sensitivity function can thus be used to predict the sensitivity of a design to manufacturing errors, or it can be used in an optimization cycle of a gun's design.

articleTitle: Recent advances in high-power metamaterial microwave sources at UESTC
abstract: Metamaterials are a new type of artificial materials engineered to have some exotic properties such as Reversed Cherenkov radiation (RCR). Due to the attractive advantages such as high-power, high-efficiency, miniaturization, and easy fabrication, metamaterial microwave sources have been developed at University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC). In this talk, we first introduce the RCR and report the recent advances in the RCR experiment. Secondly, two kinds of S band high-power metamaterial microwave sources are reported. Finally, their potential applications are addressed.

articleTitle: Design and experiment of A 340 GHz traveling wave tube for terahertz cloud radars
abstract: The 340 GHz traveling wave tube is being developed for the terahertz cloud radar. The device is designed to produce 1 W output power. It uses a pencil electron beam focused by PPM and a microfabricated folded waveguide slow wave structure. The first prototype has achieved 50 mA of transmission current but there is no amplification due to the immense loss. After redesign and improvement of the slow wave structure, the loss of the latest prototype is much lower. The latest prototype will be tested soon.

articleTitle: The modal analysis of high-frequency circuit in microwave tube based on finite element method
abstract: The reliability and stability of the high-frequency circuit (HFC) in microwave structure affect the overall performance of the microwave tube directly. During use the microwave tube, various mechanical shocks and vibration stresses make the dynamic performance of the HFC in microwave tube very strict. It is significant to project corresponding numerical simulation software used in optimize the structure design of microwave tube. In this paper, using the finite element method, a software package Mechanics Simulator for modal (MCS-M) which is a part of Microwave Tube Simulator Suite (MTSS) and can be used for modal analysis of HFC in microwave tube was developed. To validate MCS-M, numerical results for a helix slow-wave structure is shown compared with ANSYS.

articleTitle: Simulation and measurement of a W-band circular TE62 mode generator for gyrotrons
abstract: In this paper, a circular TE62 mode generator is simulated and measured in order to test the quasi-optical mode converter system, which would be used in a W-band gyrotron with TE62 mode. The mode generator sequence is rectangular waveguide TE10 - coaxial waveguide TE61 - cylindrical waveguide TE61 - rotating TE61 mode - rotating TE62 mode. Simulation and calculation of the mode generator has been achieved. The optimum converting efficiency of the desired mode is approximately 90%. The output field pattern of the mode generator is presented in a temperature-sensitive liquid crystal display (LCD) sheet by the low-power microwave.

articleTitle: Study on the dispersion characteristics of sine waveguide based on the field match method
abstract: In this paper, a proper theoretical model is proposed to investigate dispersion characteristics of the sine waveguide slow-wave structure. Based on the proposed model, the dispersion equation is obtained utilizing the field matching method. Through numerical calculation, dispersion characteristics are calculated and the results agree well with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Nano-CNC fabricating Y-band folded waveguide backward wave oscillator
abstract: We present simulation results on a Y-band folded waveguide backward wave oscillator (BWO). Since the finalized circuit will be fabricated by nano-computer numerical control machining, we obtained its parameters from analytic equations with considering cutting tool's dimensions. Depending on the different number of periods, BWO's generated frequency and power were obtained. A cold test and hot test of the circuit is discussed in simulation level.

articleTitle: Investigation of microwave sensor on the planar mushroom-shaped metamaterial
abstract: The investigation of microwave sensor on the planar mushroom-shaped metamaterial is considered. The results of numerical simulation microwave sensor for measurement of physical quantities and monitoring parameters of technological processes using CST Studio Suite are presented. Also it is shown that the microstrip sensor has geometrical dimensions much smaller operating wavelength while maintaining a high Q-factor structure.

articleTitle: A 140 GHz gyro-amplifier using a dielectric-loaded, sever-less confocal waveguide
abstract: We report results of the high gain operation of a pulsed 140 GHz gyro-amplifier system under development at MIT for pulsed Dynamic Nuclear Polarization NMR (DNP-NMR). With a 46 kV, 3 A beam, the gyro-amplifier operated with 23 dB of device gain at 140 GHz, measured from the input port to the output port. With input / output coupling losses estimated at 12 dB, the gain of the confocal circuit itself is estimated to be 35 dB at 140 GHz. The gyro-amplifier uses a sever-less, confocal geometry to provide an overmoded interaction circuit with reduced mode competition. Higher gain has been achieved by including ceramic absorbers in order to attenuate unwanted oscillations due to spatial modes that are reflected from the outer vacuum tube wall.

articleTitle: Advanced, phase-locked, 100 kW, 1.3 GHz magnetron
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research, Inc., in collaboration with Fermilab and Communications & Power Industries, LLC, is developing a phase locked, 100 kW peak, 10 kW average magnetron-based RF system for driving accelerators. Phase locking will be achieved using an approach originated at Fermilab [1] that includes control of both amplitude and phase on a fast time scale.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a multiple-beam extended interaction oscillator with coaxial structure
abstract: The applications of multiple-beam in the Extended Interaction Oscillator with coaxial structure permits a significant increase in the average output power at high frequencies. The EIO circuits suitable for the multiple-beam interaction are designed in a coaxial structure. The analysis of this newly developed circuits shows it can interaction with the multiple-beam efficiently. To demonstrate this capability, a Ka-band EIO with coaxial structure has been designed. A five-beam with a total current of 5 A (evenly divided among five beams) at a voltage of 25 kV was used in this device. Simulations with a 3-D PIC-code predict an output power up to 22 kW at 34.5 GHz, the efficiency is about 17.6%.

articleTitle: Automatic test system for electric parameters of traveling wave tube
The MetOp-SG SCA high power amplifier
abstract: MetOp-SG is a cooperative undertaking between ESA and EUMETSAT. The wind scatterometer (SCA) payload will be on board the Satellite-B (Sat-B) and is a real-aperture C-band radar with a peak output power of 2.2 kW, pulse length of 1.15 ms and a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 32 Hz. In this work, the development and design of the klystron based High Power Amplifier (HPA), which is a central unit of SCA, is presented. While Airbus DS acts both as instrument prime and as HPA prime, the klystron is developed by Communications and Power Industries (CPI), Canada.

articleTitle: First experimental observation of plasma breakdown for detection of radioactive material using a gyrotron in real-time
abstract: A gaseous plasma avalanche phenomenon is one of candidates to discover a radioactivity in long-distance. A minimum lag time composed of mainly formative delay time and statistical delay time is essential to initiate the plasma volume discharge. Based on the delay time distribution, the existence of radioactive material is determined. In this paper, we present experimental results on the reduced delay time with radioactive source.

articleTitle: A 94–96GHz 100 watts folded waveguide TWT
abstract: The paper introduce a W-band folded waveguide traveling wave tube(TWT), the test result show the impulse wave output power is above 100W within 2GHz bandwidth from 94GHz to 96GHz. The peak power is 120W and the maximum gain is 41.6dB. The electron efficiency is more than 3.7 % and the total efficiency is more than 18% with two stage depression collector. The tube is tested under the electron gun voltage is 19.1 KV and beam current is 145 mA.

articleTitle: Discrete model of a folded-waveguide traveling-wave tube
abstract: Folded waveguide (FW) is a promising type of slow-wave structure (SWS) for millimeter-wave traveling-wave tubes. A modified discrete model to obtain cold characteristics parameters of the FW SWS is developed. Cold characteristics such as dispersion characteristic and interaction impedance show reasonable agreement with the results of full electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a multilayer output window for a 372 GHz gyro-TWA
abstract: An output window for application in a gyrotron traveling-wave amplifier (gyro-TWA) operating at a center frequency of 372 GHz is designed and simulated. The window is based on the multilayer design and has the requirement of greater than -30 dB reflection over 24 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Metal-alloyed “cold” secondary emission cathode
abstract: A short review of metal-alloy palladiumbarium cathode properties used in magnetron microwave amplifiers has been presented. The devices of this class only use secondary electron emission cathode. In order to avoid the device excitation, thermionic emission must be excluded, so, cathode works in the so-called “cold” mode. Physical properties of metal-alloyed (Pd-Ba) secondary electron emission cathodes are shortly discussed.

articleTitle: W-band sheet beam staggered double grating traveling wave tube with simplified input/output structure
abstract: Using a simplified input/output (I/O) structure, a sheet beam traveling wave tube is designed, producing 644W at 94 GHz with a corresponding gain of 38.1 dB. And the 3-dB bandwidth is more than 12.7%. A uniform longitudinal magnetic field of 1 T was used in the PIC simulation. CST simulation results of the S parameters of the I/O structure and the port signals of the PIC model in 50ns are shown in the paper.

articleTitle: Measurement of a W-band gyro-TWA experiment based on a helically corrugated interaction region
abstract: Measurements of an upgraded W-band gyro-TWA with a helically corrugated waveguide and a cusp electron gun are presented. With upgraded input coupler and output systems a gain of ∼37 dB was measured from the experiment with a maximum output power of over 2 kW. The amplification from the gyro-TWA was measured in the frequency range of 90 GHz to 96 GHz.

articleTitle: Measurement of an upgraded input coupling system for W-band gyro-TWA
abstract: A gyrotron traveling-wave amplifier (gyro-TWA) operating at W-band has been upgraded and experimentally measured. In this paper, the design and measurement of the upgraded input coupling system for the gyro-TWA is presented. In the measurement, the transmission coefficient of the coupler is at an optimal level of about -1 dB.

articleTitle: Calculation of the interaction impedance by differentiation the “hot” dispersion equation
abstract: A simple method of the interaction impedance calculation is offered in this paper. It is shown that the differentiation in respect to the transverse constant of the “hot” dispersion equation, i.e. in the presence of the electron beam, excludes the necessity of calculation the power flow in the considered TWT model. The application of the offered method is demonstrated on the diaphragm waveguide and the sheath helix.

articleTitle: Progress in developing a high efficiency IOT for ionospheric heating
abstract: We report progress on the development of a high-power, high-efficiency source for a moveable ionospheric heater. The source is based on the Inductive Output Tube concept. The application requires operation in the 3-10 MHz range, thus opening the possibility to achieve true class - D operation and with that high efficiency. Our designs incorporate a solid-state driver, a grid-less gun, and a tunable output circuit. Preliminary results on a scaled device will be presented.

articleTitle: 3D modeling of a sheet-beam sub-THz traveling wave tube
abstract: Results of 3D modeling of the 0.2 THz double-grating half-period staggered slow-wave structure are presented. A fast and accurate finite edge elements technique for simulation of broadband input/output couplers is developed. Beam focusing in a uniform magnetic field is simulated showing very good beam transmission. Small-signal and large-signal gain regimes are simulated using CST Particle Studio 3D code.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling analysis of 0.31 THz TWT based on a double-grating rectangular waveguide
abstract: In this paper we analyzed the 310 GHz TWT based on double-grating rectangular waveguide with circular beam channel and square beam channel. Comprehensive consideration, we used the square beam channel. The PIC simulation shows that the output power is more than 10W in demand bandwidth 305-315GHz, meet the technical parameters requirements.

articleTitle: Multimode steady-state analysis for a Ka band Gyrotron Traveling Wave Amplifier
abstract: In this abstract, the analysis for improving the stability of Gyrotron Traveling Wave Amplifier with Uniform Dielectric-Loaded (UDL) and Periodic Dielectric-Loaded (PDL) waveguides was studied by multimode steady-state theory. The realization process of the steady amplification for a Ka band TE01 fundamental mode Gyro-TWT was discussed. The theoretical results for the RF output power are in good agreement with those in the experiment at a 7% velocity spread.

articleTitle: A modified microstrip meander-line slow wave structure for planar traveling wave tubes
abstract: In this paper, a modified microstrip meander-line (MML) slow wave structure (SWS) for planar traveling wave tubes (TWTs) is described with the analysis of its dispersion characteristics, interaction impedances and transmission properties. Compared with conventional MML SWS, the modified SWS has wider cold band with an increased rate of about 53.5% and larger interaction impedances (21.4% increased). What's more, the metal MML has better connection with the dielectric rod, which improves stability and reliability under thermal shock, stress impact and electron bombardment.

articleTitle: A BWO based on novel metamaterial slow-wave structure
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel metamaterial slow wave structure (SWS) for backward wave oscillator (BWO) to develop the high power microwave source. The high frequency characteristics of the SWS are analyzed by the HFSS, the transmission properties and the beam-wave interaction process are simulated in the CST Studio Suit. The simulation results reveal that the BWO based on the novel metamaterial SWS can produce 0.552MW output power and an interaction efficiency of 9.84% at the typical frequency of 31.6GHz.

articleTitle: Stability study of a broadband, two-gap MBK input cavity using the klystron code TESLA-MB
abstract: We present the results of a study of the stability of a two-gap input cavity used in an experimental broadband multiple-beam klystron (MBK) with 18-beams and 7-cavities, which was designed for projected > 500 kW maximum output power and 13% bandwidth (NRL MBK-3). The device was experimentally observed to be prone to self-excitation at beam voltages below its design operational value of ~42 kV. Postexperiment examination of the two-gap input cavity revealed traces of breakdown on its face. Subsequent 3D CEM code simulations showed the presence of a high Q higher-order mode (HOM) TM11. To explore this HOM instability in greater detail, we applied the 2D parallel large-signal code TESLA-MB, which represents a parallel extension of the klystron code TESLA suitable for the accurate modeling of multiple-beam devices.

articleTitle: Novel schemes of powerful FEM-oscillators and amplifiers for potential applications
abstract: The paper describes recent results of theoretical and experimental studies of novel schemes of FEM-oscillator and amplifiers carried out in collaboration between JINR (Dunba) and IAP RAS (N. Novgorod) based on induction linac LIU-3000 0.8 MeV / 200 A / 200 ns and aimed on topical applications, including accelerating and bio-medical applications, etc. At the present stage, efficient operation of the JINR-IAP FEM-oscillator has been demonstrated at 20 MW / 30 GHz and 5 MW / 60 GHz powers. Experimental studies of a multimegawatt power 90 GHz FEM are currently in progress. The key components of these FEMs are a short period tapered wiggler responsible for high-quality helical electron beam formation, and an advanced Bragg resonator based on coupling of propagating and quasi-cutoff waves, which improves selectivity and allows advance of the FEM into short wavelengths. To achieve a broad amplification band in the FEM-amplifier we utilized the so-called grazing incident regime, in which about of 20 MW of output power was simulated in the frequency band of 30 ± 2 GHz. During the first stage of the experiments, the designed power level and fast frequency tuning in the band 30 ± 0.5 GHz (limited by utilized input signal) have been demonstrated. According to the simulations, the use of the regime of non-resonant trapping in tapered wiggler would allow an enhance in the output power up to 35-40 MW with simultaneous widening of the amplification band. Experimental realization of this novel FEM-amplifier scheme is also currently in progress.

articleTitle: The development of K-band space travelling wave tube
abstract: This paper introduced the development of 120 watt K-Band space TWT, which has global efficiency more than 58%and saturated gain higher than 50 dBin 18.4-21.2GHz frequency band. The simulation results and the main measured technical characteristics have provided in details.

articleTitle: Investigation of a 210 GHz spatial harmonic magnetron using 3-D particle-in-cell simulation
abstract: A 40-vane THz Spatial Harmonic Magnetron (SHM) at 210GHz with a cold secondary emission cathode is investigated by the use of a 3-D Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulation. There are two important features of this simulation. The one is that the electromagnetic oscillation grows naturally from the noise which enables us to observe time-evolved space charge distribution. The other is that the fabrication tolerance is taken into account in the simulation model in order to get accurate simulation results. This simulation work reveals that the SHM in THz band has a low efficiency due to the surface-wave RF field and the space charge is turbulent and appears non-periodic due to the electron secondary emission.

articleTitle: Helix traveling-wave tube interaction simulation with CST particle studio
abstract: A commercial K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>-band tapered helix traveling-wave tube is modeled and simulated in CST Particle Studio on a desktop computer. Efficient models for the electron beam, the severs and the delay line are investigated. The results of particle-in-cell simulation in CST Particle Studio are presented and compared to those of the specialized steady-state simulation code MVTRAD.

articleTitle: Modeling oscillations in TWTs using the TESLA family of codes
abstract: We report recent advances in the development of the TESLA-family of codes, with a focus on algorithms to model self oscillations in TWT amplifiers. The TESLA codes operate essentially in the frequency domain, making it a challenge to find unstable modes without prior knowledge of their frequency. As a rule, codes that operate in the time domain, such as Particle-in-Cell (PIC) codes are a more natural choice as a tool to explore the stability of beam-driven devices. However, the extensive computer resources required for PIC simulation as compared with those needed for hybrid codes such as TESLA, motivate the development presented here. The new capability to model self-oscillations in TWTs by using the TESLA family of large-signal codes is illustrated by TESLA-FW modeling of an experimental G-band serpentine TWT amplifier.

articleTitle: Microfabrication methods for a 233 GHz traveling wave amplifier
abstract: We present the application of UV-LIGA and CNC micromachining to development of a 233 GHz hybrid serpentine waveguide Traveling Wave Tube amplifier. Results compare achievable resolution and tolerances, and electromagnetic cold testing measurements. Output power from the TWT amplifier is predicted to exceed 140 W from a 20 kV, 124 mA electron beam.

articleTitle: The progress of 3-dimensional particle-in-cell code CHIPIC
abstract: The capacity and progress of 3-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) code CHIPIC, which is based on the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, is reviewed. CHIPIC has been developed for more than one decade, starting from simulating vacuum devices. During the last decade of development, the functionality of CHIPIC is extended from 2-dimension to 3-dimension, from text interface to graphical interface, from serial computation to parallel computation, from simple boundary condition to multiple boundary conditions, and from electron-only PIC simulations of vacuum devices to complex plasma particle-in-cell/Monte Carlo collision (PIC/MCC) simulations of various devices.

articleTitle: Experimental research on Ka-band TM02 mode RBWO with low guide magnetic field
abstract: An overmoded relativistic backward-wave oscillator (RBWO) operating in TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> mode is researched experimentally. It is found that the large radius ratio of the outer and inner conductors in the diode region improves the operation stability in the low magnetic field. And reducing the diode gap enhances the microwave generation. In experiment, the microwave pulses with the power 286 MW in Ka-band are obtained. The pulse shortening is mainly cause by the bombardment of the stray electrons on the device surface.

articleTitle: Mini-TWT in gain and phase matched applications
abstract: A gain and phase matched traveling wave tube (TWT) e2v-GPMT operating over a band of 7.5-18GHz with a minimum output power of 60W is presently under production at e2v. The present design is based on an existing mini-TWT that incorporates a focus electrode switching gun, a phase velocity tapered helix slow wave structure, a single stage depressed collector, an SMA input and a TNC output connector. During development and pre-production stages a number of tubes were manufactured and their performances were matched. In this paper we have described gain and phase matching techniques of such devices. Experimental results of a number of matched devices have been collated that show a gain match within ±3dB and phase match within ±15°.

articleTitle: A mode discrimination method for multi-gap cavity of sheet beam klystrons
abstract: The multi-gap planar resonant cavity can provide a stronger beam-wave interaction for sheet beam klystrons, whereas, how to exactly discriminate the working mode is always a difficult thing in the practical coldtest process. Based on the perturbation theory, we have put forward an effective mode discrimination method to distinguish the working mode from the non-working ones and the interference signals. As a demo of its validation, a copper multi-gap cavity model is machined and tested, the measurement data, the simulation, and the theoretical predication exhibit the highly consistent variation of the frequency offset. This method could be very useful in the frequency adjustment of the concerned mode in the multi-gap cavity of sheet beam klystrons.

articleTitle: Pre-development of a C-band klystron intended for synthetic aperture radar in space application
abstract: A C-band klystron has been developed at Leonardo company, based on an European Space Agency (ESA) contract, targeting a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) instruments that are essential for Earth Observation application. The paper presents the design features of the klystron, with particular emphasis on the main critical parameters (RF performances and potential multipaction issues). The development has been concluded with an elegant breadboard (EBB) fully representative of the klystron design. The test results on these models are presented; they demonstrate the capability of the design to meet the target requirements. The view expressed herein can in no way be taken to reflect the official opinion of the European Space Agency.

articleTitle: Improved field emission from tungsten doped reduced graphene oxide
abstract: The emission capability of as prepared reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and tungsten doped reduced graphene oxide (W-rGO) film field emitter (FE) cathodes are investigated experimentally. It is observed that W-rGO films showed a highest emission current density of ∼ 800 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at an applied DC electric field of 6.6 V/μm, which is far superior than the current density of ∼ 390 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> from an as prepared rGO film. Short stability test also showed that emission current is much more stable than the rGO films. These excellent improvements can be attributed to the doping of tungsten into the rGO film, which helped to repair the broken bonds thus lowering the turn on field. Also, tungsten gives the film an excellent mechanical stability and higher thermal load handling capability, which is very important to achieve a stable, high performance operation and long life.

articleTitle: Large scale production of advanced high current density thermionic cathodes
abstract: Large scale production of high current density thermionic cathodes based on nano-composite scandate tungsten technology is under development. When produced with high quality, this material offers an order of magnitude higher current density than what is currently available commercially. To address manufacturability of the high-performing material in quantities of over 100 kg per year, a quality controlled production process for nano-composite powder and sintered pellets has been initiated. Completion of this commercialization program will provide the vacuum electronics industry immediate access to high quality advanced cathode material that is evaluated by UC Davis and independently confirmed by L-3 Electron Devices, Teledyne MEC, CPI, SLAC, JPL, and Ceradyne, a 3M Company.

articleTitle: Dispenser cathodes for e-beam lithography machine: A quick take
abstract: Several dispenser cathodes with microscopic emissive area, including ones with anti-emissive coating, have been tested for application in e-beam lithography tools. Major requirements were high loading, >15 A/sq.cm, and uniform profile of the emitted beam. Some of the cathodes tested came close to meeting these lithography specs.

articleTitle: A multiple-hole input coupler for a 372 GHz gyro-travelling wave amplifier
abstract: The design of a multiple-hole coupler that operates at a center frequency of 372 GHz for use in a gyrotron traveling-wave amplifier (gyro-TWA) is presented. In simulations, the coupler achieved 35% bandwidth from 289 GHz to -410 GHz with transmission losses of -0.5 dB predicted.

articleTitle: Origination of oscillation startup in RBWO from radiation of electrons
abstract: In this paper, the radiation of electrons during the oscillation startup in the relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO) is investigated theoretically. It is found that the initial power of an X-band RBWO is in level of 1 μW, and the output power reaches up to 1 GW in 6~16 ns. The theoretical results agree with particle-in-cell (PIC) results to some degree. The theoretical method can be used to analyze the radiation of the electron beam and microwave power of other RBWOs at the beginning of startup.

articleTitle: A super-wide band output circuit with two channels for klystron applications
abstract: A super-wide band output circuit with two channels for klystron applications are proposed. In S band, a broadband circuit with 550MHz bandwidth has been designed and experimented through tuning a designed switch on the coupled slot of a double gaps coupled-cavity (DGCC) for realizing two channels. The results of cold test accord with the simulated results very well.

articleTitle: Design of transverse field sweeping system for W-band gyrotron collector
abstract: This paper designed a transverse field sweeping system (TFSS) based on the electromagnetic theory for W-band gyrotron collector. The optimum simulation results with TFSS are obtained and indicate that the range of spent beam spread and the peak power density are about 370mm and 130W/cm2, respectively.

articleTitle: Study on the after cavity interaction in a 140 GHz model TE0,3 gyrotron using 3D CFDTD PIC simulations
abstract: The dynamic after cavity interaction in a down-scaled gyrotron model has been studied using a 3-D conformal finite-difference time-domain particle-in-cell simulation. The purpose is to identify whether this effect is physical or artificial and might be taken into consideration when designing the uptaper and launcher.

articleTitle: Mode-locked electron oscillator based on two coupled helical gyro-TWTs
abstract: Based on a time-domain model we demonstrate that a periodic train of powerful ultrashort microwave pulses can be generated in an electron oscillator consisting of two coupled helically corrugated gyrotron travelling wave tubes (gyro-TWTs) operating in regimes of amplification and saturable absorption, respectively. Mechanism of pulse formation in such an oscillator is based on the effect of passive mode-locking widely used in laser physics. Saturable absorption can be implemented in a gyro-TWT in the Kompfner dip regime by a proper matching of the guiding magnetic field. According to simulations with the parameters of an experimentally realized Ka-band gyro-TWT, the peak power of generated pulses with duration of 200 ps can achieve 400 kW.

articleTitle: Towards an 2 MW long-pulse coaxial-cavity gyrotron: Progress on the advanced KIT inverse magnetron injection gun
abstract: An innovative Inverse Magnetron Injection Gun (IMIG) has been designed at KIT. This IMIG will be employed in the modular KIT 2 MW, 170 GHz coaxial-cavity pre-prototype gyrotron. The specific design allows the implementation of a significantly larger emitter ring compared to the “conventional” MIG, considering the same radial dimensions. Due to the direct cooling of the thermally loaded components close to the emitter a significant better temperature profile for those components is achieved. A significant smaller thermal expansion of the electron beam forming components is achieved and the possibility for unwanted emission is reduced. Hence, an excellent electron beam quality under gyrotron operation can be expected. This contribution shows the progress on the manufacturing, assembly and testing.

articleTitle: Phase retrieval of high-power gyrotron orbital angular momentum beams
abstract: We present an effective phase retrieval technique for determining the vortex charge of a high-power orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam based on phase coefficients optimization. The high-power OAM beam is generated by transmitting a 25 kW, 95 GHz Gaussian like gyrotron beam through a spiral phase plate (SPP). Determination of the vortex charge of the OAM beam is carried out using a modified phase retrieval algorithm. Retrieved intensity profile show 99.27% intensity regeneration at measurement planes for the high-power OAM beam.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave extended interaction oscillator based on pseudospark-sourced electron beam
abstract: In this paper the study of a W-band extended interaction oscillator based on a pseudospark-sourced electron beam will be presented. This new device successfully produced a peak output power of over 38 W, which agrees well with the prediction from the 3D particle-in-cell simulation. It displays the outstanding features of compactness and cost-effectiveness. The main contributing factors include the transport of the electron beam by the positive ion focusing channel without the need of an external guiding magnetic field and high interaction impedance and high gain per unit length of the extended interaction oscillator circuit.

articleTitle: Tunable high-power microwave source based on the squeezed state of relativistic electron beam
abstract: In this work we investigate numerically processes of microwave generation in virtual cathode oscillator (VCO) containing hollow intense relativistic electron beam (REB) with an overcritical current in the regime of squeezed state formation. We show the squeezed state of REB that acts like a dense active electron media to demonstrate good generation properties from the viewpoint of VCO frequency increase. Typical values of microwave generation frequency are higher than 10 GHz. Along with the studying of generation characteristics we analyze in details the emergence and development of diocotron instability in the REB squeezed state which leads to formation of vortex structures.

articleTitle: W-band klystron upconverter driven by pseudospark-sourced electron beam
abstract: In this paper, a three-cavity klystron upconverter operating at W-band is presented. It is predicted to generate 40 W when driven by a 30 kV, 0.2 A electron beam. Pseudospark-sourced electron beam after post-acceleration was proposed to be used with the klystron upconverter because it has the advantage of low energy spread, high current density, and no need of any external guiding magnetic field.

articleTitle: Electron optics system for a Ka-band extended interaction klystron
abstract: The design and calculation of an electron optics system for a Ka-band extended interaction klystron was described. A cylindrical electron beam with voltage 25kV, current 2.5A was generated by a convergent Pierce type electron gun and was confined by a uniform permanent magnet focusing structure. The design was accomplished by using the 2-D gun code EGUN and 3-D gun code Opera.

articleTitle: Recent advances in beam optics analyzer
abstract: This paper will present recent progresses and advances in Beam Optics Analyzer including its geometric entity based post-processing of field data, adaptive meshing capability to efficiently model hollow beams as those in magnetron injection guns, and optimization of the X-ray spot size.

articleTitle: TWT model on a meta-magnetic plate
abstract: A TWT model formed by a meta-magnetic plate and a metal screen is offered and analyzed. The dispersion equation of the model in the presence of a homogeneous electron beam filling the space between the plate and the screen is derived and solved. The coupling and depression coefficients are calculated by the method of differentiation the dispersion equation. The calculated characteristics are compared with the TWT models on a dielectric plate and an “impedance” comb.

articleTitle: Landmine detector on a slow-wave structure
abstract: A novel method of landmines detecting is offered in this paper. The method is based on “pumping” electromagnetic energy from a slow-wave structure in a surrounding medium at the phase velocity exceeding the light speed in the medium. This effect was approved in the physiotherapy and now is offered for detecting the landmines, including the plastic explosives hidden in the soil. Physics and the expected properties of the offered detector are described.

articleTitle: A low voltage Ka-band mini traveling-wave tube
abstract: This paper describes a Low voltage Ka-band Mini-TWT. The TWT is set up for a 5.6 kV cathode voltage with a nominal beam current of 65mA, packaged configuration of no bigger than 175mm×42mm×23mm and weight of less than 0.35kg. Dual depressed collector is used in the design of this TWT. As a result, within 32-37GHz, the TWT can achieve the saturated output power of greater than 40W and the efficiency of great than 25%.

articleTitle: Millimeter and THz range chaotic ultra-wideband generation in gyrotrons
abstract: We demonstrate the possibility of ultra-wideband (UWB) chaotic generation in the large-orbit 30 kV/0.7A gyrotron, operated at the 1st, 2nd and 3rd cyclotron harmonics. According to a time-domain averaged model and 3D PIC simulations, the spectrum width of output radiation can achieve 10.7, 5.3 and 2.5 GHz at the frequencies of about 117, 240 and 350 GHz, correspondingly.

articleTitle: Simulation the electron transport characteristic of GaN photocathode
abstract: In this paper the electron transport characteristic of GaN photocathode is simulated. After the electrons got across the band bind region and reached to the cathode surface, the distributing of electron energy is 2.3~3.4 eV. And the surface electron escapes probability of GaN photocathode with different energy is changing with the structure of surface barrier. The barrier I is more impotent that affecting the surface electron escapes probability than that of barrier II, its structure is determined the electron transport characteristic. And in the vacuum, the electron energy that corresponding to the peak electrons number is 2.95 eV..

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave periodic surface lattices for mode control in vacuum electronic sources
abstract: Periodic surface lattice (PSL) structures of planar geometry have been designed, constructed and measured. The motivation is to study the evolution of electromagnetic fields stimulated by PSLs to improve mode control in overmoded structures in high power electron beam driven THz vacuum electronic sources. The results of studies of the planar structures are presented. Prior to the experimental studies numerical simulations have been carried out and results are compared with experimental measurements. It is demonstrated that volume and surface fields can couple so as to form a cavity eigenmode, which has the potential to be selectively and efficiently excited.

articleTitle: Double reversed U shaped meander line slow wave structure
abstract: We report the design and simulation of a double reversed U shaped meander line (DR U-ML) slow wave structure (SWS). The DR U-ML SWS has two U-ML with reversed symmetric in one unit. The simulation results show that the pierce impedance of DR U-ML is 15% higher than that of U-ML and the dispersion fluctuation in working frequency is 0.02c of DR U-ML compared with 0.06c of U-ML. The simulation results show that the DR U-ML is suitable for broadband TWT design.

articleTitle: Development of a multiscale model for the field electron emission properties of carbon-nanotube-based carbon fibers
abstract: A multiscale array model has recently been presented to describe field electron emission (FE) from carbon nanotubes (CNTs) on the apex of a carbon nanofiber (CNF) fabricated as a CNT aggregate. The model considered Joule heating, radiative cooling and Henderson/Nottingham cooling/heating, assumed CNT destruction at a specified tip temperature, and predicted the CNT fraction destroyed as a function of macroscopic field, and related current-voltage characteristics. The model reproduces features observed in recent experiments on FE from CNFs, including the emission current order-of-magnitude (mA range), the low turn-on field (fraction of V/μm), deviation at high field from the pure Fowler-Nordheim behavior expected for an undamaged CNT array, loops in current-voltage characteristics, and spatial variation of temperature along the CNF. Here, this array model is used to explore how some details of the CNT arrangement at the fiber apex (especially statistical variations in CNT geometry) might affect overall emission characteristics.

articleTitle: CPI SNS Klystron lifetime and reliability analysis
abstract: Communications and Power Industries, LLC (CPI) klystrons are populating the majority of sockets in the superconducting linac of the Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The klystrons are rated for 550 kW or 700 kW peak at 805 MHz. The klystron production and factory test data provided confidence the device would provide reliable service. Seventy nine sockets have an accumulation over 5.5 million hours of filament operation and 5.0 million hours of high voltage operation to date. Only 3 klystrons have been removed from service since linac conditioning began in 2004.

articleTitle: An equivalent circuit analysis for staggered double-grating slow-wave structure
abstract: In this abstract, an equivalent circuit for the staggered double-grating slow-wave structure was discussed. The formulae of dispersion and coupling impedance were obtained. The calculations for the dispersion and coupling impedance show that the results of the equivalent circuit are in rational agreement with those of the CST-MWS simulation.

articleTitle: The study of AM/PM coefficient in Helix TWT
abstract: The AM/PM coefficient has been simulated in a C-band Helix TWT with Microwave Tube Simulation Suite (MTSS). The results of the simulation show that pitch and rod width play a significant role of affecting AM/PM coefficient. And the AM/PM coefficient has been reduced by 3.484 deg/dB after optimization.

articleTitle: Factory test results of the L-3 L6200 multi-beam IOT for the European spallation source
abstract: L-3 Electron Devices has successfully completed factory testing of the L6200 1.2 MW Multi-Beam Inductive Output Tube (MBIOT) for the European Spallation Source. The ten-beam, permanent magnet-focused device meets the maximum 1.2 MW output power specification at 704.42 MHz with a DC-to-RF efficiency of 68.4%; efficiency is maintained above 60% down to 650 kW. The gain at 1.2 MW exceeds 21 dB. No oscillations were detected at any point during operation. The MBIOT is currently being prepared for shipment, after which it will undergo long-duration life testing.

articleTitle: Field emission study of small number of carbon fiber field emitters
abstract: Experiments and simulation were performed to study the emission characteristics of small number of field emitters. The experiment consists of nine carbon fibers in a square configuration. Voltage-current traces were obtained and compared to four carbon fiber emitters in a linear and square configurations as well as to two carbon fiber emitters in a paired array.
