Results shows that the turn-on voltage is always larger for the nine carbon fiber emitters as compared to the two and four emitters in linear configuration, and approximately identical to the four emitters in a square configuration. The observations suggest that electric field screening effects depend strongly on the number of emitters, separation between them as well as their geometrical configuration.

articleTitle: Spurious emission and Arc suppression in electron guns
abstract: Electron guns for RF sources typically use barium dispenser cathodes to produce electron emission. Barium and oxygen diffuse to the emission surface whenever the cathode is hot to replace that lost by evaporation. The barium combines with the oxygen to form barium oxide, which reduces the surface work function. Barium that evaporates from the surface is deposited on nearby surfaces, including grids and high voltage electrodes. If the barium recombines with oxygen, it can result in spurious electron emission and arcing from these surfaces. This research is investigating surface coatings to suppress spurious electron emission from these surfaces by preventing barium oxide formation.

articleTitle: Using of reflections for expansion of frequency tuning in a THz-band gyrotron
abstract: Effect of delayed reflection on operation of a second-harmonic THz-band gyrotron is studied. Theoretical analysis, numerical calculations and experimental observations for the 0.394 THz FU CW IIB gyrotron are presented.

articleTitle: Broadband waveguide port matching in Neptune
abstract: We demonstrate a method to obtain a second-order absorbing boundary condition for propagating, broadband, electromagnetic waves in 3D electromagnetic-PIC simulations, that does not introduce spatial derivatives of the fields and that is therefore straightforward to implement. For power propagating in a TE mode of a waveguide (of arbitrary cross-section) the method achieves a numerical reflectance below -25dB, for frequencies 3% or more above the respective mode cut-off frequency. This capability is critical to the reliable prediction of stability in vacuum electronic amplifiers, where spurious numerical reflections in simulated waveguide ports can artificially enhance instabilities at any frequency. We present the theory and verification using NRL's GPU-accelerated PIC code, Neptune.

articleTitle: Decoupling techniques in high-power magnetrons with coaxial output
abstract: The adoption of a coaxial output in high-power magnetrons can lead to significant coupling between the cathode and the output disc or aerial. RF power can travel out of the anode, along the cathode, as a result of this coupling. Two techniques to achieve suitable decoupling, thus reducing the power flowing in the sidearm, have been studied by computer modelling, and the results will be shown in the following.

articleTitle: Field electron emission theory for technology
abstract: The process of field electron emission (FE) is relevant to several technological applications of interest to vacuum electronics. In such contexts, it is helpful to be able to accurately simulate the electron emission process itself and (where relevant) the behavior of technological devices and processes based on FE. It is also necessary to be able to correctly interpret the results of experimental investigations into the behavior of specific field emitters. A fully realistic theory of FE would be intensely difficult in its fine details, and full understanding seems well beyond the existing frontiers of theoretical physics. Nevertheless, over the last ten years there has been significant progress in physical and mathematical understanding. This paper aims to give a high-level overview of these developments and how they improve our ability to understand and simulate field emitter behavior in technological contexts.

articleTitle: A high efficiency S-Band klystron for medical accelerator system
abstract: With novel techniques and research on the klystron bunching method, 10% increase in efficiency is expected in S-band high-perveance klystron. Different bunching strategy is compared in this work, and a plug-compatible tube is fabricated to verify our high efficiency design.

articleTitle: Continuing production of the DBS band, 1,250 watt peak power superlinear® helix TWT
abstract: Throughout 2016, Communications and Power Industries (CPI) has been continuously manufacturing the VTU-6398D9C: a compact, high peak power, high linear power, high efficiency, and conduction-cooled helix vacuum electron device. The TWT was developed in 2015 to serve the burgeoning DBS Satcom market. As the number of units produced grew in 2016, and continues to grow, CPI has learned the new product has very repeatable performance and can be produced with a high yield. However, the higher volume has revealed a few areas where improvements can be made to tighten distributions at the subassembly and piece part level. These adjustments and refinements have been put in place and are producing new results. Performance margins are increased and unit to unit variations are decreased. Higher volume rates in 2017 can be realized.

articleTitle: Development of a 5-18GHz, 150W TWT
abstract: A traveling wave tube (TWT) operating in the frequency band 5-18GHz with output power 150W is presently under development at e2v. The design of the tube has been carried out using an existing mini-TWT as a baseline. To start with, a number of codes available commercially and developed internally have been validated experimentally to establish their suitability in using them for design purpose. These codes have been used to design the TWT and sensitivity analysis of each component to set the dimensional tolerances. This paper presents experimental validation of codes, design methodology and experimental results of the TWT.

articleTitle: Investigation of a planar metamaterial slow wave structure for traveling wave tube applications
abstract: In this work we report the design of a novel planar slow wave structure based on a metamaterial architecture. The dispersion characteristics and the electric field distribution within the structure will be presented. The slow wave structure was designed to be used in traveling wave tube amplifiers operating in W-band. Preliminary PIC simulations were performed showing a gain of 22 dB for the TWT amplifier. The accuracy of fabrication, low fabrication costs and small dimensions make this new structure very appealing for the realization of TWT high amplifiers for wide area wireless networks with high data rate.

articleTitle: Development of the ultra-wide band millimeter wave TWT with two stage SDV-SWS
abstract: The development of the high output power and ultra-wide band Millimeter wave travelling wave tube (TWT) using staggered double vane slow wave structure (SDV-SWS) combined with planar alignment electron beams are investigated in this paper. It is found that the first two modes of SDV-SWS can be used simultaneously to match with the same electron beam energy to promote the beam-wave interaction bandwidth greatly. Also the novel two stages SDV structures are incorporated to suppress the beam-wave interaction oscillation effectively. Particle in cell (PIC) simulations with planar alignment three beams SDV-TWT can produce over 2.12 kW of peak power with the 3dB bandwidth of 28 GHz in W-band. And the sheet beam SDV-TWT in G-band can also produce over 590W of peak power with the 3dB bandwidth over 70 GHz.

articleTitle: High performance of x-ray tube with field-emission cathode
abstract: Gate grids and CNT field emitters have been studied deeply to improve the performance of x-ray tube with field-emission cathode. In order to obtain clear x-ray image with low dosing, a narrow pulsed current with high peak value has to be generated in the x-ray tube. In order to reduce the electrons collected by gate electrode, the graphene is covered on the gate grids as electron transparent film. The gate grids are also coated by the dielectric film with high secondary electron yield to enhance the anode current further. Apart from this, the carbon nanotubes are used as field-emitters here. The adhesion of CNTs on the substrate is enhanced with metallic particles, so the pulsed emission with high current is quite stable. Consequently, the peak value of pulsed current on the anode is improved obviously. Finally, a few clear x-ray images for moving objects are obtained.

articleTitle: Study of virpertron — Vircator with dielectric inserts
abstract: We propose a novel approach for the design of virtual cathode oscillator in this work. As a new concept, we suggest the microwave system containing annular relativistic electron beam travelling through the drift space with dielectric inserts characterized by different values of permittivity. In this case, virtual cathode which is the source of powerful electromagnetic oscillations forms at the junction of different dielectric materials. According to the mechanism of virtual cathode formation, we have called this device as “virpertron”. We have carried out the detailed numerical investigation of virtual cathode formation features in this system via 3D electromagnetic PIC-simulation. We have also studied the spectral properties of the microwave radiation generated by virpertron.

articleTitle: Developments of the MICHELLE charged particle beam optics code for high performance computing
abstract: The existing HPC capabilities in the MICHELLE ES PIC code is being supplanted with new distributed-memory, MPI-based domain decomposition and per-node accelerators such as GPUs and multicore processing. New interfaces are also being built between MICHELLE and existing DOD software tools such as CAPSTONE, GSB, and ParaView to form the next generation framework for efficient design and optimization workflow. This is an evolutionary process, and this paper reports on the latest progress and discusses applicable algorithms and implementations.

articleTitle: Emission profile of a miniature source on conductive plane
abstract: It has been shown, theoretically and experimentally, that miniature emitter located on conductive plane would have loading higher than predicted by “three-halves law”, and its emission profile would be that of “inverted Gaussian”, i.e. emission current density at the edges would exceed that in the center. Engineers using cathodes of this type should know actual current density distribution rather than its average figure.

articleTitle: Generation of powerful ultrashort sub-THz pulses based on cyclotron superradiance
abstract: We demonstrate the possibility of generation of multi-megawatt sub-THz pulses based on cyclotron superradiance (SR) from bunches of electrons rotating in a strong magnetic field. For selective excitation of an operating mode in oversized waveguide the regime of group synchronism, when the wave group velocity is close to particle translational velocity, should be used. Theoretical analysis was performed in the frame of average approach and confirmed by direct 3D PIC simulations.

articleTitle: 20MWp High-efficiency L band multi-beam klystron for CLIC drive beam
abstract: THALES ELECTRON DEVICES (Thales ED) has developed and is currently manufacturing a new highly-efficient L band Multi-Beam Klystron (Model TH1803). This klystron has been designed in the frame of CLIC project and the main challenge for this amplifier is to achieve the high efficiency target of 70% required by CERN. The klystron design and available test results will be reported.

articleTitle: Study of a rectangular beam extended interaction klystron in G-band
abstract: A multi-gap ladder-type resonant cavity with rectangular beam is designed for G-band extended interaction klystron (EIK). The periodic long-gap and short-gap alternated is applied in this structure. By theoretical analysis and optimal design, the structure parameters of cavity working at π mode are finally obtained. Through PIC simulation of six-cavity model, the results show a good output stability and mode competition suppression. With the operating voltage 16.5 kV, operating current 0.30 A and driving power 50 mW, the output power 271 W, efficiency 5.5% and 3dB bandwidth 670 MHz is achieved.

articleTitle: The numerical error analysis of trace ripple simulation in strong bunching in TWT
abstract: In this paper the numerical error of trace ripple simulation in TWT is first presented, which is happened in nonlinear interaction region especially in strong bunching and will ultimately lead the error calculation of the beam-wave interaction. Then the reason is discussed, and some efforts to suppress the numerical error has been shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of a 346GHz high harmonic traveling wave tube
abstract: Base on the electronic beam can generate high harmonic signal after modulated by electromagnetic wave, a novel high output power terahertz source has been designed-The terahertz high harmonic traveling wave tube. Simulation result shows the device cover bandwidth of 338GHz-350GHz with power around 100mW when the input signal is from 84.5GHz to 87.5GHz with power around 100mW.

articleTitle: L & S-band family of space qualified TWTs
abstract: L-3 Technologies Inc. (L-3), Electron Technologies Inc. (ETI) has recently developed a family of L & S-band traveling-wave-tubes (TWTs), offered in both conduction-cooled and radiation-cooled configurations. The family is space qualified and capable of producing between 130 and 325 W of saturated RF power at efficiencies exceeding 70%. Current production of the recently qualified 325 W, radiation-cooled, waveguide output S-band space TWT utilizes this family architecture, resulting in improved procurement, yield and cycle times while maintaining the performance and reliability L-3 ETI is known for.

articleTitle: Advances in supercomputer optimization of RF devices
abstract: An integrated environment for large scale multiparameter design optimization of RF devices is presented based on AFRL's Galaxy Simulation Builder (productivity tool for distributed high performance computing), Sandia Lab's DAKOTA (local and global optimization tool), NRL's CAPSTONE (meshing) [1], and Leidos' MICHELLE (electrostatic particle-in-cell code). The environment leverages high-end parallel computing resources for rapid optimization of complicated problems.

articleTitle: Computational design and optimization of a magnetron injection gun
abstract: Gyrotron traveling wave tube (gyro-TWT) is mainly electronic beam transverse energy and electromagnetic wave energy exchange. So the high quality electronic beam must have a sufficient pitch factor α (v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>/v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>). A modulating anode with curved geometry was designed and the multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) was employed to optimize the curved geometry. A high pitch ratio of 1.57 and a low velocity spread of 0.6% were obtained. A sensitivity analysis with respect to critical parameters, such as magnetic compression ratio, anode-cathode distance and anode spacing, has been carried out.

articleTitle: Optimum design of output cavity in 0.34 THz EIK
abstract: The output cavity used in 0.34 THz extended interaction klystron (EIK) is developed and optimized by using theoretical analysis and numerical simulations. Beam-loading conductance is researched by using the small signal theory and the cavity is accordingly optimized to contain eight gaps. Considering of transmission coefficient and feasibility in manufacture, the tapered coupler is presented and the issue of mode competition is discussed. The physical design is simulated and verified by particle-in-cell (PIC) technology finally and the results show that an output power of 143 W can be reached at the frequency of 347.7 GHz, approaching the gain of 37.7 dB.

articleTitle: Broadband HE04 mode exciter for W-band confocal Gyro-TWA
abstract: A new method to excite HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">04</sub> mode in wide bandwidth for W-band confocal gyrotron travelling wave amplifiers (gyro-TWAs) is presented. The mode exciter consists of a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sub> mode exciter and a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sub>-HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">04</sub> mode waveguide transition section. Numerical results show that the mode exciter achieves an optimal transmission of -0.55 dB and a relative 3 dB transmission bandwidth of ~17%. The mode exciter shows broad bandwidth and flat transmission characteristics. Besides, it is compact and easy to be fabricated, which can be applied to cold test experiments of the interaction circuit.

articleTitle: High performance uncertainty quantification analysis of RF devices
abstract: We present a high-performance, integrated environment for uncertainty quantification (UQ) and reliability analysis (RA) of Vacuum Electronic RF devices based on Sandia National Lab's DAKOTA toolkit, NRL's GPU-accelerated, 3D Electromagnetic PIC code Neptune, and AFRL's Galaxy Simulation Builder productivity tool for distributed high-performance computing. The environment allows for UQ studies of RF devices to be incorporated in the device design process and to be deployed, carried out, monitored and analyzed in an efficient, user-friendly, robust, and flexible manner, using a diverse variety of high-end parallel computing resources.

articleTitle: Field emission cells with high aspect ratio of glassy vertical emitters and electron guns based on them
abstract: The results of the research of the field emission cells with a large aspect ratio of vertically-oriented emitters made of glassy carbon for use in microwave devices are presented. The possibility of developing electron optical systems (EOSs) with field emission cathode matrices for microwave devices such as O-type microwave tubes is shown.

articleTitle: Development of W band folded waveguide traveling wave tube
abstract: A W band folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube that adopts horseshoe-shaped attenuator and a periodic step-tapering folded waveguide slow wave structure is reported in this paper. In this Traveling Wave Tube, Reflection from severability was effectively reduced and self-oscillation was depressed, and also electronic efficiency is raised by about 1.5~2% comparing with uniform periodic folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube.

Author Keywords: w band folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube

articleTitle: Possibilities of using reverse focusing system in klystron with variable electron beam energy
abstract: The results of the electron beam formation and transportation simulations in the multibeam klystron (MBK) with reverse focusing system operating with variable control electrode (grid) or anode voltages are presented in this paper. The possibility of using multibeam klystrons for supplying acceleration systems, running with various electron beam energy or power is shown.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of a high efficiency relativistic backward wave oscillator
abstract: An X-band overmoded Relativistic Backward Wave Oscillator (RBWO) with non-uniform Slow Wave Structure (SWS) and Resonant Reflector (RR) is designed to increase the beam-wave interaction efficiency of RF and slow space charge wave. The problem of pulse shortening is overcome by using overmoded SWS to some extent. The 3D simulations of the RBWO show that with a diode voltage of 600kV and beam current of ~4.3kA, a microwave power of 1.40GW at 9.24GHz is obtained. The power conversion efficiency of more than 50% is obtained due to the use of overmoded non-uniform SWS as compared with conventional RBWO.

articleTitle: Set of microwave devices with CW output power 2 and 4 MW on 2.45 GHz frequency
abstract: Block diagram and parameters of the set of microwave devices with CW output power 2 and 4 MW on 2450 MHz frequency have been described. The set of devices is intended for heating high temperature plasma in installations like tokamak. High output power is provided at the account of adding up powers from 24 CW klystrons with output power 100 and 200 kW in the working vessel of a tokamak.

articleTitle: Initial design of RF system for an L-band klystron
abstract: The ring beam klystron has advantages of both annular beam klystron and multiple beam klystron. In this paper, an RF system with sector ring beams for L-Band klystron is described. The output power attains to 10MW with input power of 500W.

articleTitle: I. The progress of 346GHz BWOs
abstract: 346GHz backward wave oscillations (BWOs) have been considered as a key device for fusion plasma diagnostics, whose development is a joint project under collaboration among Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Institute (BVERI), University of California Davis (UC Davis) and Lancaster University. In this paper, we report on some progress being made in the development of a 346GHz BWO.

articleTitle: Development of an advanced vector analysis code for simulation of electromagnetic fields in quasi-optical systems of high power gyrotrons
abstract: An accurate and fast simulation tool for the analysis of quasi-optical output couplers in high power gyrotrons is under development. The electric field in the quasi-optical system is described by the electric field integral equation (EFIE) which is numerically solved by a Galerkin-type method of moments (MoM). To accelerate the simulations, a set of first order basis functions for curved triangles and the adaptive cross approximation algorithm (ACA) are used. The quasi-optical mode converters are parametrized by local B-Splines which can approximate launcher walls with perturbations very well. To speed up the calculations for highly oversized geometries, the software implementation supports parallelization on shared- and distributed-memory systems.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the fast diffusion process of the collector plasma in the relativistic backward wave oscillator
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the diffusion process of the collector plasma in the relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO) by means of numerical simulation. The results show that there is a fast diffusion process of the collector plasma, corresponding to a plasma electron velocity of 20 cm/ns. In this process, the plasma affects the modulation of the intense relativistic electron beam (IREB), leads to microwave frequency drift, absorbs the microwave power on an order of GW levels, and finally causes the pulse shortening. Here, mechanism of the fast diffusion process is mainly attributed to the excessive plasma density and the standing wave pattern of microwave field in the interaction region.

articleTitle: Study of interaction of two gyrotrons with time-delay coupling
abstract: Coherent operation of several gyrotrons is important for power combining applications, especially for electron-cyclotron resonance plasma heating. In this paper, a model of two coupled gyrotron oscillators is developed and basic regimes of the mutual interaction are studied. Time delay of the coupling signal traveling between two gyrotrons strongly affects the pattern of phase-locking regimes.
