articleTitle: 2nd Harmonic Gyrotron simulation with CST STUDIO SUITE®
abstract: The 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic operation of a Gyrotron is very attractive as the B-field can be reduced by half. However, due to the sensitivity of this operation, it is challenging to simulate this efficiently in a 3D Particle in Cell (PIC) code. This paper shows aspects to keep in mind when simulating a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic Gyrotron within the PIC code of CST STUDIO SUITE®.

articleTitle: A high power polarization converter based on rectangular aperture frequency selective surface
abstract: A transmission type high power polarization converter which could convert a linear polarization to circular polarization is proposed in this paper. In order to meet application requirement of the high power, the polarization converter is realized by a metal frequency selective surface based on the rectangular aperture. The rounded edge angle of the unit is used to help the power capacity of the proposed structure. The performance of the polarization converter is investigated, and the simulation results shows that the Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) is less than 2 from 33GHz to 40GHz, the 3 dB axial ration bandwidth is about 4 GHz. The proposed polarization converter features high polarization purity, low cross-polarization level, simple structure, and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: Design and parametrs of CW klystrons with output power 100-200 kW on 2.45 GHz frequency
abstract: The design and parameters of CW klystrons with output CW power 100–200 kW, operating on 2450 MHz frequency are described. The specific feature of klystrons is the use of one dimension-type of a solenoid for focusing. Calculated data for the klystron with output CW power 300 kW and results of exploiting these devices in tokomak for heating high-temperature plasma are presented.

articleTitle: Experiments on sub-teraherz folded waveguide traveling wave tubes
abstract: Taking advantage of X-ray LIGA system, we fabricated sub-teraherz folded waveguide circuits. Small signal gain in a W-band folded waveguide TWT was measured to be 15 dB. Folded waveguide circuits operating at both 220 GHz and 850 GHz were fabricated. Cold tests shows 10 dB return loss and 6 dB transmission characteristics of circuits in G-band.

articleTitle: Optimised permanent magnet focusing system for Sub-THz clinotrons
abstract: We propose to use composite permanent magnet and iron insert focusing system for modern compact sub-THz vacuum electron devices of the clinotron type that has the potential of improving by at least a quarter on the mass of the current in-house design while preserving the required values of guide magnetic field, simplifying the system assembly, and reducing the overall system dimensions.

articleTitle: Metal-tip-array field emission cathodes for X-ray tubes
abstract: Metal-tip-array field emission cathodes with non-integrated mesh gates are proposed to be the electron sources for X-ray tubes. The cathodes theoretically have better emission uniformity than carbon nanotubes (CNTs) cathodes which are most used in field emission X-ray tubes and work more stable than cathodes with near-integrated gate. The cathodes are fabricated mainly based on Spindt cathodes process in present and the process is expected to be simplified in further research.

articleTitle: Terahertz large-orbit high-harmonic gyrotrons at IAP RAS: Recent experiments and new designs
abstract: We describe new versions of high-harmonic gyrotrons with axis-encircling electron beams developing on the basis of two (80 keV pulsed and 30 keV CW) experimental setups. Selective operation at the second (0.267 THz) and at the third (0.394 THz) cyclotron harmonics were observed in the 30 keV gyrotron. Quasi-regular cavities with periodic phase correctors, where a far-from-cutoff axial mode with a decreased diffraction Q-factor is excited in a gyrotron-like regime, are designed to improve the operation at the third harmonic, as well as to achieve the fourth-harmonic operation at frequencies of up to 0.65 THz. At the pulsed gyrotron setup, a sectioned klystrontype cavity with a decreased diffraction Q-factor was experimentally tested.

articleTitle: Design of a two-stage Ka-band relativistic sheet electron beam traveling wave tube
abstract: Research of a two-stage Ka-band relativistic sheet beam traveling wave tube (RTWT) is presented in this paper. The high frequency characteristics of the high frequency system and the beam-wave interaction performance are investigated, and an output power of 19.5MW is obtained. At last, this two-stage RTWT is processed and its transmission characteristics are tested.

articleTitle: Full thermal analyses for slow-wave structure in helix-TWT under operation
abstract: The temperature distribution and thermal deformation along the slow-wave structure of a travelling wave tube (TWT) under operation have been analyzed. Considering a series of thermal losses, including electron collision on the helix, eddy current loss on the surfaces of the helix and barrel, and the electromagnetic field loss in the attenuators, we analyze the full thermal status for the slow-wave structure of TWT by using CST MPhysics Studio. The simulation results show high-temperature region is concentrated on the last 15-20 turns of the helix on which the highly geometric deformation is produced, and same deformation is also generated on inner conductor of output window with the peak deformation value of 0.0157 mm.

articleTitle: Development of Ku band miniature TWT
abstract: This paper describes the development of miniature Ku-band pulsed helix traveling wave tube(VE3306) within 2GHz bandwidth. The peak power reached more than 450W and overall efficiency was 42% with 30% pulsed duty cycle. The miniature TWT can be used as the transmitter of T/R module and booster of MPM(Microwave Power Module).

articleTitle: Design and development of a novel 1,250 watt KU-band CW helix traveling wave tube
abstract: Communication and Power Industries (CPI), USA has designed, and developed a novel 1,250 Watt high power, high efficiency, compact, conduction-cooled continuous wave Helix Traveling Wave tube VTU6397J4 for Satcom application. This paper presents the test results of the two initial TWT prototypes produced. Both units were tested in a light-weight conduction-cooled baseplate, used SMA female coaxial input and WR-75 waveguide output connections as designed. Both prototypes measured over 1,300 watts of average CW output power, over 51 dB of small signal gain across the extended Ku-band from 12.75GHz through 14.80 GHz. TWT's demonstrated good linearity and third-order intermodulation performances at 4 dB and 7 dB back-offs from rated power (61.0 dBm). TWT design includes a standard proven electron Gun assembly with FE turn-on and isolated anode, a two stage multi-stage depressed collector assembly, and a novel slow wave structure. Test results are in agreement with the design goals. The predicted and measured performance data are compared.

articleTitle: Powerful multichannel planar FEMs based on intense parallel sheet beams
abstract: Novel schemes of powerful multichannel planar FEMs was developed in IAP RAS - BINP RAS collaboration based on two parallel sheet beams 0.8 MeV / 1 kA forming by the accelerator ELMI. In 75 GHz frequency band two-channel planar FEM with hybrid two-mirror resonator providing two-dimensional distributed feedback was elaborated. For record transverse size of interaction space (up to 45 × 2.5 wavelengths) synchronization of emission from both electron beams and realization of stable narrow-band generation have been demonstrated. As a result, spatially-coherent radiation with the output power of 30-50 MW and pulse duration of ~100 ns was obtained in this FEM in each channel. To advance powerful long-pulse FEM into THz frequency range original project of two-stage oscillator is under development at the ELMI accelerator. As a microwave system for such oscillator a ring cavity based on four Bragg deflectors has been proposed. Recent results of theoretical and experimental studies of this FEM scheme are presented.

articleTitle: Development of Ka-band 25 wattmini TWT
abstract: This paper describes the development of Ka-band 25Watt peak powerminitravelling wave tube (TWT) in IECAS. The mini TWT is light-weight and compact, weighing less than 200g and measuring less than 200×20×35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> unpacked. An output peak power of greater than 25W has been demonstrated in band of 33-37GHz, with the performance of more than 30dB gain and more than 37% total efficiency.

articleTitle: Field emission CNT-based electron focusing system for terahertz TWT
abstract: This report presents the results of experimental investigations of cathode-grid structure based on CNTs. The experimental samples of field emission cathode-grid array based on vertical-aligned CNT with the cell of 1 μm diameter and with 5 μm pitch of microstructure are fabricated. The electron focusing system with a sheet CNT cathode with linear convergence 14, and with the beam current density of 78.4 A/cm2 has been designed in terms of experimental data of a current-voltage characteristic of the cathode.

articleTitle: Investigation of “serpentine”-type slow-wave structures in the terahertz range
abstract: In this paper, dispersion characteristics of “serpentine”-type slow-wave structures, which are promising for the terahertz range use, are calculated. For 3D-modeling, HFSS was used. Program described in work [1] was used in the calculation. Using the obtained characteristics, octopole chain model of the slow-wave structure is constructed. Discrete approach is advisable in solving these problems [2]. Justification of the applied mathematical model for the discrete interaction follows from the difference form of electrodynamic theory of excitation [3]. Requirements to coefficients of the resulting finite-difference equation are high, because their accuracy determines how close the mathematical model of the discrete interaction to the physical laws is. These coefficients have a certain electrodynamic sense and are obtained through the octopole transmission matrix coefficients. In turn, this octopole is a mathematical model of the resonator slow-wave structure cell.

articleTitle: Filter transformer section for wide broadband in coaxial couplers
abstract: The couplers play an important role in coupling the power in and out from the helical SWS of a TWT with minimum reflection. For a space helix TWT, coupler should be wide bandwidth and small size. The main objective of the paper is to design a wide band output coaxial coupler, and a filter consisting of different radius and different length of transformer section is optimized. The simulated reflection loss of filter transformer section is obtained by using Ansoft HFSS and compares with that of three-stage transformer section. The wide band matching properties of the transformer is better than the three-section transformer section.

articleTitle: Synthesis of compressed sheet field-emission flows for terahertz TWT
abstract: The report presents synthesis method of modeling the electron-focusing systems that formed compressed sheet electron beam with supporting the beam magnetic field and field-emission cathode. Results of calculating by synthesis and analysis method of the electron gun with linear compression of the beam 10, micro-perveance of Pμ = 0.035 and 100 mA current are performed. The electron gun forms a sheet beam with a 0.125mm thickness, and 0.7 mm width.

articleTitle: Effect of circuit fabrication tolerances on the gain and phase of a W-band folded-waveguide TWT
abstract: We demonstrate a practical numerical approach to the analysis of the effects of finite fabrication tolerances on the performance of a folded-waveguide TWT. The approach involves the simulation of a numerically generated `ensemble' of TWTs that differ from each other by small random variations in certain key physical circuit dimensions. By computing the ensemble averages and standard deviations of the computed values of various performance metrics (gain, phase, and output power, for example) we can predict the average values and ranges of these and other metrics to be expected in as-built devices. Such studies also can help discover those physical dimensions to which the performance is most sensitive, and therefore can help to optimize a TWT design for maximum performance and/or manufacturing yield.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical mode converter for 1MW dual-frequency gyrotrons
abstract: A quasi-optical (q.o.) mode converter has been designed for the MW-level dual-frequency gyrotron which is under development for the upgrade of the electron cyclotron (EC) system of the TCV tokamak. The gyrotron design is essentially based on modifications of the W7-X gyrotron [1]. The launcher of the output coupler has been synthesized to adapt the geometry of the quasi-elliptical mirror with same size as in the W7-X gyrotron for both operating modes (TE17,5 @ 85GHz, TE26,7 @ 126GHz). The simulation results show that high conversion efficiencies and low stray radiations in the q.o. system can be achieved.

articleTitle: Design and development of the recirculating crossed-field amplifier
abstract: The Recirculating Planar Crossed Field Amplifier (RPCFA) is a high-power microwave device adapted from the Recirculating Planar Magnetron (RPM) [1], developed at the University of Michigan. A travelling-wave, rectangular meander line design has been developed in simulation that amplifies a 1.3 MW signal at 3 GHz to approximately 29 MW, a gain of approximately 13.5 dB, with nearly 53% electronic efficiency. The amplifier is designed to be driven by the Michigan Electron Long Beam Accelerator (MELBA), which is currently configured to deliver a -300 kV, 1-10 kA, 0.3-1.0 us pulse. The RF signal will be provided by an MG5193 magnetron which can deliver microwave pulses with a peak power output of 2.6 MW at 3 GHz for up to 5 us.

articleTitle: S band improved metamaterial slow-wave structure
abstract: In this paper, we present an S band improved metamaterial slow-wave structure (SWS), which is in order to increase the bandwidth of the previously proposed metamaterial SWS. A drift tube is added in the metamaterial unit cell, and the improved SWS has been further studied and analyzed by using Ansoft HFSS and CST Particle studio particle-in-cell solver. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of the improved metamaterial SWS has been effectively increased compared with that of the metamaterial SWS, and the peak output power of the S band backward-wave oscillator based on the improved SWS is 20.7 MW with an electronic efficiency of 92.4%.

articleTitle: Efficient excitation of high axial modes in simulations of low-voltage gyrotron
abstract: The gyrotron operation on the modes with high axial indices is an attractive method to provide the electronic frequency tuning which is desirable for DNP/NMR-aimed sub-THz devices. However, gyrotron efficiency typically drops drastically with increase of axial index of the operating mode. In numerical simulations we reveal that low-voltage operation at fundamental cyclotron resonance dramatically increases gyrotron efficiency at higher axial modes. Moreover, for magnetic fields corresponding to the gyro-TWT regime the gyrotron output power at the second and third axial modes can be even higher than at the first axial mode. Further improve of frequency tuning takes place in gyrotron with reversed direction of power output.

articleTitle: High-throughput computational screening for low work function perovskite electron emitters
abstract: Our recent computational discovery of SrVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> possessing a low work function has spurred a much larger modeling effort to search for additional, new perovskite compounds with low work function for applications as thermionic electron emitting cathodes. Here, we detail our initial progress of conducting high-throughput Density Functional Theory calculations on hundreds of perovskite compounds. After screening approximately 600 perovskite materials, we have predicted that other new perovskite materials, BaNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and SrNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, should display intrinsic (undoped) work functions of 1.50 and 1.20 eV, respectively, superior to undoped SrVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. We have also demonstrated that transition metal d-electron count can provide guidance for tuning the work function of perovskites by altering their composition.

articleTitle: Development of a spaceborne C-band klystron for the MetOp-SG mission
abstract: A compact, conduction-cooled 5.355 GHz Klystron, based on EIK technology, has been developed for use in the Scatterometer Instrument segment of the forthcoming MetOp-Second Generation mission. Two engineering model Klystrons have been built since the start of the development effort in 2016 and a full space-qualification model will follow in 2017. The Klystron draws upon space heritage from higher frequency Extended Interaction Klystrons developed for the CloudSat and EarthCARE programs, and utilizes a new RF circuit design, tailored to the MetOp-SG requirements.

articleTitle: Development of gyro-devices at IAP/GYCOM
abstract: Research activity on development of various gyro-devices at the Institute of Applied Physics of Russian Academy of Sciences (IAP RAS) and at the industrial company GYCOM Ltd is presented. Results of the development are illustrated by a number of recently fabricated and tested gyrotrons-oscillators and gyro-amplifiers operating at very different frequencies.

articleTitle: Fabrication of the 0.346 THz BWO for plasma diagnostic
abstract: Nuclear fusion is probably the most demanding challenge the scientific community is facing. The plasma is a delicate material that has to be properly shaped to achieve a high efficiency fusion process. Unfortunately, the plasma is affected by micro-turbulences still not fully understood, detrimental for the reactor functioning. The diagnostic of plasma is a fundamental technique that needs advanced approaches for a full mapping of the plasma behavior. The 0.346 THz backward wave oscillator is the enabling devices for a high-k plasma diagnostic that will provide unprecedented insight on turbulences leading to full operational fusion reactors. This paper describes the final fabrication phase of the 0.346 THz BWO for plasma diagnostic jointly performed in an international project, involving three leading institutions in vacuum electronics.

articleTitle: 71–76 GHz traveling wave tube for high data rate satellite communication
abstract: The increasing demand of high data rate is posing a high pressure to actual mobile networks. Fiber and wireless networks cover most of the populations, but there are many regions uncovered by a satisfactory service. The distribution of internet by satellite communications is already available at microwave frequency. The request of multigigabit data rate needs a wide bandwidth that only millimeter waves can provide. The band 71-86 GHz offers two sub bands of 5 GHz each suitable for satellite communications. However, due to the high atmosphere attenuation, an adequate transmission power has to be provided. The preliminary design of a 71-76 GHz Traveling Wave Tube based on the Double Corrugated Waveguide, for millimeter wave satellite communications is reported.

articleTitle: Backward-wave oscillation suppression in helix traveling-wave tubes by magnetic field tapering
abstract: Two techniques for suppressing backward-wave oscillations in homogeneous helix sections of traveling-wave tubes are presented. For this purpose, the focusing magnetic field is modified. The first technique aims at compressing the electron beam in order to reduce beam-wave coupling. The second one changes the beam rotation to affect the backward-wave interaction. Both techniques increase the margin against backward-wave oscillations significantly. Theory and simulation results are presented and compared.

articleTitle: Study of the oscillation startup time in a G-band EIO based on a pseudospark-sourced electron beam
abstract: Extended interaction oscillator (EIO) operated in the terahertz range puts greater demand on current density and brightness of electron beam. The pseudospark (PS)-sourced electron beam is a good candidate to drive such high frequency EIOs as it has a very high combined beam current density and brightness. This paper presents the numerical studies of oscillation startup time in a G-band EIO based on a pseudospark-sourced electron beam. It was found that the G-band EIO circuit's oscillation startup time and efficiency are relative to the gap length of it with the same period. The authors also present the latest results that demonstrate the successful design and optimization of G-band EIO driven by a 402 mA (500 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) PS-sourced electron beam. A peak power over 1.27 kW at 184 GHz was achieved using an electron beam, which can be generated by PS discharge.

articleTitle: Design of a 94 GHz photonic bandgap based extended interaction klystron amplifier
abstract: A complete design of a 94 GHz extended interaction klystron (EIK) amplifier has been developed at the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center. The device utilizes a novel, mode selective photonic bandgap (PBG) structure which enables the use of a modified PBG coupling scheme. Using particle-in-cell simulation, the EIK is predicted to generate 42 dB of gain and 130 W saturated power.

articleTitle: High PRF microwave power module with electronic power conditioner of enhanced features
abstract: Microwave Power Module produces high RF power in a compact package. Leonardo has a well consolidated heritage in design and production of conventional traveling wave tubes and helix mini-TWT for military naval, airborne and missile applications. Strong on his own experience Leonardo has developed wideband, 100 to 150 Watts class CW and pulsed helix mini-TWT. Based on his own helix mini-TWT Leonardo has developed a high PRF, wide bandwidth Microwave Power Module including an EPC of enhanced features. MPM architecture approach and performances are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A high efficient X-band klystron-like RBWO
abstract: A high efficient X-band klystron-like relativistic backward wave oscillator is studied. By adding a drift tube after the first period of the slow wave structure, the energy spread of the electrons decreases effectively, and the fundamental harmonic current reaches maximum in the extracting cavity. Utilizing a trapezoid resonant reflector with a ridge, the depth of pre-modulation could be adjusted continuously. As a result, the beam-wave interaction is promoted greatly and the efficiency reaches 65%.

articleTitle: Study of a 1.5 KW average output power CC-TWT with a 10% banwidth operating in X-band
abstract: A three-section coupled cavity TWT is under development for avionic application. The design parameters point out for a TWT in X-band with an high average power, high power, high efficiency, high duty, wide band, low weight and rugged structure. Data are presented which show as preliminary results of simulations are in agreement with the tests on each RF section. The simulations have been done with a software developed in house for the evaluation of the impedance interaction and use of CST suite has been done for the prediction of the dispersion diagram.

articleTitle: The design and calculation of P-Band 1.2MW multi-beam Klystron
abstract: Comparing with single beam klystron, Multi-Beam Klystron (MBK) can operate at low beam voltage, and has small volume and weight. To satisfy the requirement of high energy proton accelerator for Spallation Source and ADS (Accelerator Driven Sub-critical System), the design and calculation of a P-band 1.2MW MBK was made in Institute of Electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IECAS). By using 30 beams, P-band MBK can work at beam voltage of 35 kV with cathode loading of <;2.5A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. By using 5 cavity (one of them is second harmonic cavity), the P-band MBK can obtain peak power of 1.282MW, efficiency of 69.7 %, and gain of 45.6 dB with length of the interaction section (600mm). It makes the total length of MBK less than 2000mm. The design consideration and calculation results are present in the paper. Also the comparison among MBK, Multi-Beam-IOT, and single beam klystron was made.

articleTitle: Inductive meandered line metamaterial for metamaterial-enhanced resistive wall amplifiers
abstract: The metamaterial-enhanced resistive wall amplifier (ME-RWA) has been demonstrated, through theory, to be a high gain wideband amplifier. This work presents the design and preliminary cold test results of a constructed ME-RWA. In this ME-RWA design, the metamaterial consists of a periodic arrangement of inductive meandered lines. To verify the properties of the metamaterial, the structure's dispersion was measured and found to be in good agreement with simulation and theory.

articleTitle: 220GHz confocal waveguide Gyro-TWT with double lossy severs
abstract: A 220GHz Confocal Waveguide Gyro-TWT with double lossy working on HE06 mode is designed. With related basic theories, the parameters of confocal waveguide is studied. Based on these parameters, the dispersion curve are calculated. Then, lossy sever confocal is adopted to suppress backward oscillation. Two schemes are explored: single lossy sever, and double sever severs. Both experiments and PIC simulations show that single lossy sever is not enough to suppress backward oscillation for this gyrotron, while Gyro-TWT works well by enough self-oscillation suppression of double lossy severs. For this 220GHz double lossy severs gyro-TWT, PIC simulations show that the peak output power is 10.7kW, the peak efficiency is 11.65%, peak gain is 25.5dB and the 1dB bandwidth is 2.3GHz. Keywords: confocal waveguide, gyro-TWT, particle-in-cell, double lossy severs.

articleTitle: Design of helix slow-wave structure for Ka/Q dual-band TWT
abstract: The design of fan-shaped metal loaded helix slow wave structure for a dual-band (Ka/Q) traveling wave tube is presented in this paper. The beam-wave interaction simulation predicts a minimum output power of 199/191 W, minimum electronic efficiency 15.1%/12.5%, and maximum gain of 50.1/49.9 dB, respectively, for Ka-band(29-31GHz) and Q-band(43.5-45.5GHz).

articleTitle: Relativistic charged-particle beam limiting current in bounded coaxial drift tube
abstract: We obtain the analytical estimate of space-charge limited (SCL) current of axisymmetric relativistic charged-particle beam in coaxial drift tube bounded in the longitudinal direction. Numerical nonlinear and analytical estimates of SCL current in the finite drift tube are compared.

articleTitle: An estimation method of inner temperature distribution of TWT slow-wave structure with GA-BP neural network model
abstract: An estimation method for inner temperature distribution of slow-wave structure is proposed without placing temperature sensors inside the traveling wave tube. The inner temperature distribution is estimated based on body temperatures, with Genetic BP Neural Network solving the thermodynamic parameters of the thermal model. The results showed that the method has good accuracy and feasibility.

articleTitle: Non-adiabatic electron optical system with field emitter for a spectroscopic gyrotron
abstract: We propose a new concept of the electron-optical system for a gyrotron for spectroscopy application, where the primary electron beam appears due to the field emission. Requirements to the choice of the design of a multi-pin cathode are substantiated. The shape of the electrodes and the geometry of the magnetic system, which provide the formation of a helical electron beam with parameters suitable for the gyrotron operation are found.

articleTitle: Design of 220GHz folded waveguide traveling wave tube based on theory and simulation
abstract: In this paper, a 220GHz folded waveguide traveling wave tube (FW-TWT) was designed based on theory and simulation. Firstly, the FW-TWT was analyzed by small signal theory. The small signal gain varying with the beam voltage and current was solved by the small signal theory. Then the FW-TWT was simulated by the Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. The output power varying with voltage and frequency was simulated. According to the theory calculation and simulation, the performance of the 220GHz FW-TWT can be predicted.

articleTitle: Design of two beams gun and folded waveguide slow wave in 0.14THz traveling wave tube
abstract: As Terahertz communication technology developed, the research for 0.14THz folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (FWTWT) require higher power and wider band. The design and simulation on the two beams FWTWT was presented, including two beams electronic-gun, two circuits Folded Waveguide Slow Wave Structure (FW SWS). The simulation for electronic-gun is obtained two beams emission in operating voltage 15kV. The single beam current is calculated 40mA. Two circuits FW SWS are analyzed, including power splitter and combiner and sever. The combined power efficiency is about 99%. By the simulation, the combined output power is about 56W in frequency 0.14THz. The gain is 31.4dB and 3dB bandwidth is 7GHz.

articleTitle: Method of elimination of a high-order mode in the overlapping-mode double-gap output circuit
abstract: This paper describes a self-oscillation phenomenon which was detected during the course of hot-test of an S-band klystron. In order to eliminate the self-oscillation, the further simulation of the Overlapping-Mode Double-Gap Output Circuit (OMDGOC) was carried out. The electric field distributions of high-order modes and the electric conductance were analyzed and calculated, respectively. The self-oscillation might be aroused by the electric field of TM420 mode, and an absorbing cavity for decreasing the electric field was taken into account. A new OMDGOC with absorbing cavity will be fabricated and cold-tested, and then it will be validated through the further experiments with a specialized klystron.

articleTitle: Accelerated life test method for storage vacuum electron device based on pressurization
abstract: This paper proposes an accelerated life testing method for the storage vacuum electron device (VED) based on pressurization and establishes an accelerated life model. The accelerated life test of a VED is performed at 4.5 atm. The result showed that after pressurization the cathode current dropped faster than that when the VED was stored in air. The pressurization could accelerate the VED storage life.

articleTitle: Design of a output structure for Ka-band Gyro-TWT
abstract: A output structure, consists of a down taper, a 90 degree waveguide bent, and a corrugated waveguide horn, which can output the Gaussian beam rather than the operational TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0, 1</sub> mode is proposed for Ka band Gyro-TWT. The simulation results show that the mode purity of output Gaussian mode over than with the mode conversion over than 96% at the window from 30GHz to 39GHz. The outputted linearly polarized Gaussian mode could be directly usable for low-loss transmission as well as for effective antenna feeding and no extra mode converters are needed.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the high harmonic traveling-wave tube
abstract: A new type of vacuum millimeter wave source-high harmonic traveling wave tube (HHTWT) fabricated and tested. The prototype tube shows 350mW@133.5GHz was delivered with 300mW@44.5GHz input signal. The beam voltage is 18.4kV and the beam current is 86mA. The experiment proved the high harmonic amplification can be realized in TWT. It provide a new way to obtain high power, wideband tunable terahertz radiation.

articleTitle: Analysis of vane-loaded three-beam folded waveguide slow-wave structure for 220GHz TWT
abstract: Two vane-loaded three-beam folded waveguide structures, the symmetrical vane-loaded structure and the staggered vane-loaded structure, are proposed in this paper. Simulation results show that, for 220GHz traveling wave tube (TWT), the stagger vane-loaded structure has better cold characteristics and beam-wave interaction characteristics than those of the symmetrical vane-loaded structure.

articleTitle: Investigation of RF and DC plasma electron sources for material processing applications
abstract: This work presents the design, development and experimental results obtained from an RF plasma cathode Electron Beam (EB) gun for material processing applications. EB currents of up to 38 mA at -60 kV were extracted and correlated to Optical Emission Spectroscopy (OES) measurements. OES measurements and Argon II ratios were used to compare hollow and flat electrode designs as well as to examine changes in other key plasma parameters (i.e. plasma pressure and excitation power). The spectroscopic measurements and Argon II ratios indicated a higher ionization rate for the hollow electrode geometries and plasma parameters that generated larger EB currents (i.e. higher excitation power and lower pressure). The RF plasma cathode gun was compared to a DC plasma cathode gun. The DC plasma cathode produced larger currents than the RF plasma chamber. This result agreed with the OES measurements, which showed a higher ionisation in the DC plasma.

articleTitle: Study of 220GHz relativistic BWO with phase velocity taper
abstract: In this paper, a 220GHz relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO) with phase velocity taper is studied. The RBWO with phase velocity taper consists of five parts, including two parts of slow wave structures (SWS) which have different dispersion characteristics, the cathode, the resonant reflector and the output waveguide. The single-grating rectangular waveguide is selected as the SWS. Based on an RBWO without phase velocity taper, another part of SWS with different dispersion characteristic is added to build an RBWO with phase velocity taper. With the phase velocity taper, the output power of RBWO achieves 9.68MW at 220GHz, which increases 20% by the RBWO without phase velocity taper.

articleTitle: A study of fourth-harmonic multiplying gyrotron traveling-wave amplifiers operating at different frequency multiplications
abstract: A comparative analysis of fourth-harmonic multiplying gyrotron traveling-wave amplifiers (gyro-TWAs) with three schemes of operation is presented. The simulated results show that the gyro-TWAs are most susceptible to the fundamental harmonic TE11 competing mode, regardless of the operating scheme, and the mode-selective circuit can provide an attenuation of more than 20 dB to suppress the competing modes. The amplification of the wave in a gyro-TWA depends on the lengths of sections, and the gain increases for all schemes as the length of the lossy section or the length of the copper section increases. All schemes exhibit almost same saturated output powers and bandwidths while the saturated gain of the scheme at a high frequency multiplication ratio is less than that of the scheme at a low frequency multiplication ratio. Extensive numerical calculations of the power and gain scaling are conducted for all schemes.

articleTitle: S band metamaterial-based sheet beam device
abstract: In this paper, we present an S band metamaterial-based sheet beam device. The performance of this device is studied by particle-in-cell simulations and hot experiments. The simulated results indicate a ~2.85 GHz microwave signal with ~1.8 MW peak output power is generated at the output port near the cathode. Meanwhile, the measured results show that the signal has ~650 kW peak output power at ~2.87 GHz. The facts show that this metamaterial-based sheet beam device can be developed to a novel high-power microwave source.

articleTitle: Elastic thermal deformations in EOS units measuring and simulation
abstract: This paper presents the results of the thermal movement measurements of cathode-heating unit (CHU) details for a powerful C-band multi-beam klystron. There are also the numerical simulation results of the CHU, that shows the good agreement between the experimental and the calculated data.

articleTitle: Design of a 0.13THz folded-waveguide TWTA
abstract: We present a preliminary design of a 0.13THz folded-waveguide (FW) traveling-wave-tube amplifier (TWTA). The beam-wave interaction is simulated using a 1-D large signal code, BWISFW-1D, which uses a three-port network representation of the unit cell of the slow wave structures. The simulated output power is in excess of 55W from 128-138GHz, and the maximum efficiency is 4%.

articleTitle: Radiation of multibeam microwave generator on electron-oscillator flows
abstract: Spatially distributed generators on electron-oscillator flows are promising for high-power microwave radiation. In the case of multibeam generator output microwave energy of each beam can be made via antenna assemblies that determine the polarization of the field including a linear polarization in one direction of the coordinate axes. By the method of the non-linear nonstationary theory developed the discrete model of the multibeam microwave generator based on use of the equivalent self-oscillators with slowly varying amplitudes and phases. Formation of an antenna radiation field in three-dimensional approximation on the example of cylindrical ring system of radiators is considered. Each ring consists of a large number dipoles oriented in the longitudinal direction.

articleTitle: Experimental realization of W-band relativistic gyrotron with 5 MW output power
abstract: The relativistic gyrotron with thermionic magnetron-injection gun was developed and experimentally tested at 3-mm wavelength band. The gyrotron yielded stable generation of the rotating TE12,5,1 mode of a circular waveguide cavity with 250 kV/100A helical electron beam. The mode was transformed into the Gaussian wave beam by a built-in mode converter. Output power of the gyrotron was over 5 MW in pulses with durations of about 0.5 μs.

articleTitle: Scattering matrix analysis of a high-power pill-box-type window without ghost mode
abstract: Using Scattering Matrix Analysis Method (SMAM), a high-power pill-box-type window without ghost mode is designed and simulated with a VSWR less than 1.1 in its frequency band (2.8-3.8GHz). Furthermore, the relative convergence of this scattering matrix analysis method has also been analyzed. The results show that the mode number no less than 100 is proposed for this complex window. Finally, the S-parameters calculated by this method are compared with that from CST simulation and the results are found to be in quite accordance. Worth noticing, comparing with CST, this method requires less memory.

articleTitle: Phase focusing and synchronization of microwave generator with electron-oscillator flows
abstract: As part of simplified three-dimensional problem studied the self-excitation of the finite portion of the active medium on electron-oscillator flows at centrifugal electrostatic focusing. In addition to the study of the transverse motion of the electrons in each ensemble considered longitudinal movement and interaction of a large number of ensembles displaced in the longitudinal direction. Radiative interaction in multibeam microwave generator with electron-oscillators held by centrifugal electrostatic focusing leads to phase self-focusing in ensembles of oscillators and to rise of the dipole moment of the system over time. In the presence of feedback across the field this process leads to self-excitation of the small volumes of the active resonant medium and obtaining stationary generation. The impact of noise on the input of a flow determines the width of the spectral line. Radiative coupling of individual generators accompanied by their mutual synchronization and narrowing of a range of radiation.

articleTitle: The analysis and improvement of the magnetron cooling channels
abstract: A new anodes cooling channel of a high-power continuous wave magnetron is designed and it improves the properties of magnetron cavity including strain, stress, temperature distribution and resonant frequency by comparing with the original cooling system with simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Two-surface multipactor in a coaxial transmission line
abstract: Multipactor effect in a coaxial transmission line was studied theoretically and numerically. The results show that significant radio frequency breakdown likely originates from gas desorption in the material and further gas ionization induced by electrons. The multipactor effect using different surface gas pressures was analyzed with particle-in-cell simulations. The simulation results indicate that plasma originating from locally desorbed gas causes significant power reflection and absorption. At the same time, plasma electrons play a more significant role than plasma ions in the multipactor process. A numerical method such as the one used here can thus be used to predict whether radio frequency breakdown can be caused by the multipactor effect.

articleTitle: Unambiguous determination of the wave impedance
abstract: The unambiguous determination of the wave impedance is offered and approved in this paper. It is shown that in the case of slow-wave structures, the wave impedance ambiguity is caused by the longitudinal capacitive currents. They decrease the effective value of the voltage applied to the conduction current in the impedance electrode. This is followed by the decrease in the real power flow and leads to the ambiguous determination of the wave impedance by the conventional formulas of the circuit theory.

articleTitle: Design of low voltage folded waveguide multiple beam mini-TWTs
abstract: Design methodology for low voltage high power multiple beam Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) amplifiers with folded waveguide (FW) slow wave structure (SW) has been developed. Four beam multiple beam (MB) FW TWT operating at 6.2 kV with power per beamlet about 75 W and total power of 300 W has been designed and studied by using NRL large signal codes TESLA-FW and CHRISTINE-FW and NRL GPU based PIC code Neptune. Recent status of experimental demonstration of MB mini TWT in NRL also will be presented.

articleTitle: Methods of coherent summation of microwave superradiance pulses generated in independent channels
abstract: We develop two approaches for coherent summation of Cherenkov superradiance (SR) pulses in order to obtain generation of electromagnetic fields of extremely high intensity. The first method is associated with correlating the phase of SR emission to the sharp edge of a current pulse, while the second approach is related to initiation of Cherenkov SR by an initial ultrashort seed rf pulse. In this paper we present the theoretical model describing both approaches alongside with results of experiments.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit model of Terahertz folded waveguide traveling wave tube
abstract: In this paper, the transmission characteristics of the folded waveguide traveling wave tube (FW-TWT) is analyzed. The FW is equivalent as the transmission line. Both the bending part and beam tunnel are considered. According to the characteristics of two-port network, the S parameters can be calculated from the transmission matrix. The CST simulation is used to compare with the theory calculation. Both single period and multiple periods are considered in the calculation.

articleTitle: Ion cyclotron resonance heating transmitter opening switch upgrade
abstract: Diversified Technologies Inc. (DTI) has installed a high-power solid-state opening switch upgrade package to replace the mercury ignitron crowbars in the Ion Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ICRH) Transmitters at MIT Plasma Fusion Science Center's (PFSC) Alcator C-Mod, a Tokamak-type fusion experimental device.

articleTitle: Study of AlN-FeSiAl microwave attenuating ceramic
abstract: Little research has been done on the Ka-band wideband microwave attenuation ceramics. In this paper, the new idea of combining AlN and FeSiAl materias is proposed: the new composite microwave attenuation ceramic materials are prepared by hot pressing sintering process, and the materials are used to characterize electromagnetic parameters. Studies indicates that under the 26.5~40GHz, and FeSiAl weight content is set to be 10wt% and 15wt%, the ceramics possess excellent broadband attenuation performance.

articleTitle: Q-band 120 watts high power traveling wave tubes
abstract: In this paper we report on the development of a millimeter wave (MMW) broadband high power traveling wave tube (TWT). Specifically, the development of a solid state vacuum device (SSVD™) based Q-band TWT that covers the bandwidth of 38-42 GHz with a saturated power of around 120 Watts will be presented. Our SSVD™ technology employs solid state integrated circuit design and fabrication for the beam-wave interaction circuit slow wave structure (SWS) to realize and achieve high performance MMW TWTs. The Q-band SSVD™ TWT uses a novel coupled cavity type beam-wave interaction circuit SWS ideal for microfabrication manufacturing and high power at MMW high frequencies. The Q-band SSVD™ based TWT is designed with a cathode voltage of less than 10 kV. This Q-band SSVD™ based TWT has a gain of 40 dB and capable of driving a milliwatt-level solid state driver to 120 Watts. The SSVD™ based Q-band TWT has the size of 260 mm × 55 mm × 51 mm (L×W×H) and weighs around 4 pounds.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of a relativistic inverted magnetron
abstract: A high power inverted relativistic magnetron was designed and simulated using the massively parallel electromagnetic particle-in-cell code ICEPIC in conjunction with single particle smooth bore relativistic analysis. This Inverted Magnetron also known as the Inverted Magnetron Oscillator (IMO) detailed here has two design variations that will be presented, the IMO-1 and the IMO-2. Both IMO models are designed to operate in L-Band at very low magnetic fields. Common to both designs is an axial RF power extraction structure. ICEPIC simulations predict that the above features combined with the IMO's stable, robust and reliable performance in the desired mode over a large voltage range yield a class of HPM source notable for absence of downstream current loss as well as low confinement field performnce.

articleTitle: Design of a 6-18GHz coaxial coupler with mode-matching technique
abstract: Based on mode-matching technique (MMT), an analytical model with full-wave coupling for analysis of coaxial-type passive devices is established and used to design a coaxial coupler for 6-18GHz wide-band helical traveling wave tube (HTWT). In the analytical model, the complex power conservation of matching surfaces is studied deeply and the result witnesses a great compatibility. The simulation results from MMT are in quiet agreement with those from CST MWS, HFSS and MTSS. Finally, a 6-18GHz coaxial coupler with a reasonable VSWR less than 1.2 is obtained and the VSWR of the coupler connected with the HTWT is less than 1.4.

articleTitle: Parametric investigation of the multi-frequency recirculating planar magnetron
abstract: The Multi-Frequency Recirculating Planar Magnetron is a prototype crossed-field, dual-frequency, highpower microwave oscillator. The anode consists of two planar cavity arrays with design frequencies of 1- and 2-GHz. Several experimental configurations have been tested using a -300 kV, 200-300 ns voltage pulse and a 0.1-0.3 T axial magnetic field. Shots examined the impact of magnetic field non-uniformity, power generated at harmonic frequencies, and isolated oscillator operation (wherein one of the two oscillators is replaced with a smooth-bore drift region). Results are presently being analyzed.

articleTitle: Toward a statistical model of electron emission from tungsten cathode surfaces
abstract: In this work, we have begun to construct a statistical model of electron emission for polycrystalline W cathode surfaces. Construction of such a model requires knowledge of which surfaces are present, the area fractions of each surface, and the work function values of each surface. We have used Density Functional Theory to explore the effect of O, Ba and Ba-O adsorbates on W surfaces to assess the impact of these adsorbates on the work function and surface stability for several different W surface orientations. A discussion of the impact of different surface adsorbates on the surface stability and work function is presented, together with newly discovered stable Ba-O arrangements on W(011) and W(111) surfaces. Finally, a plan is presented to further develop our statistical model of electron emission and the potential impact of the model for the improved design of high power microwave electronics.

articleTitle: A pulsed depressed collector for a 5 MW S-band klystron
abstract: Design of a beam energy recovery system for application to the CPI VKS-8262S S-band klystron is presented. The multi stage pulsed depressed collector optics, mechanical and thermal design, energy recovery modulator, and experimental program will be highlighted.

articleTitle: THz undulator radiation of dense electron bunches stabilized in the negative mass regime
abstract: The use of the “negative mass” regime can provide stabilization of longitudinal size of dense short photo-injector electron bunches at long distances as well as compression of the longer bunches. This allows one to increase significantly the power capabilities of a terahertz source based on coherent spontaneous undulator emission from a short bunch. The required configuration of the magnetic field can be achieved in a specially designed undulator.

articleTitle: Study for 340 GHz staggered double-vane traveling wave tube with phase velocity taper
abstract: A 340 GHz staggered double-vane traveling wave tube (TWT) is designed in this paper. The high-frequency characteristics of the slow-wave structure are analyzed. And the results of transmission characteristics indicate that the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> is below -15 dB in the frequency range of 330-350 GHz, with ridge loaded waveguide input/output coupler and rectangular attenuator. The particle-in-cell simulation is also calculated and the results indicate that the tube can produce over 8 W output power in the frequency range from 320 to 345 GHz with an operating voltage of 21.3 kV, current of 0.04 A, and an input power of 10mW. The corresponding gain is more than 29dB. Finally, with one-step velocity-tapered method, the output power has been increased about 43% at 340 GHz with respect to the previous value.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit model of a novel ridge-loaded multiple beams folded-waveguide slow-wave structure
abstract: In this paper, a novel slow-wave structure called ridge-loaded multiple beams folded-waveguide slow-wave structure has been proposed for 0.22THz traveling wave tubes. The dispersion characteristics of the folded waveguide traveling wave tube (FW-TWT) is analyzed by applying equivalent circuit model. The FW is equivalent as the transmission line. All parts and beam tunnels are considered. Compared with the CST simulation result, it is certified equivalent circuit model for this new structure works well.

articleTitle: Nano-structured multi-layer emitters — A new and promising source of high density electron flows for miniature electronic devices
abstract: Multi-layer nano-structured emitters of a new type, providing field emission from the contact of materials with different work function were investigated. The effect of the number of pairs of layers with different work function, their thickness and the influence of contacted materials work function difference on the emission characteristics of layered cathode were determined in numerical calculations. New experimental data were obtained on the emission characteristics of the cathodes prepared from contacted layers of hafnium and platinum.

articleTitle: Simulation study of the high-order mode oscillation in a four-cavity intense relativistic klystron amplifier
abstract: The high-order mode oscillation is studied in designing a four-cavity intense relativistic klystron amplifier(IRKA). The reason of the oscillation caused by highorder modes and a method to suppress this kind of spurious modes are found through theoretical analyses and the study on the influence of major parameters of a high frequency structure (such as, the oscillation frequency of cavities, the cavity Q value, the length of drift tube section and the characteristic impedance etc.). Based on much simulation, a four-cavity Intense Relativistic Klystron Amplifier with a superior performance has been designed, built and tested. An output power of 2.22 GW corresponding to 27.4% efficiency and 61 dB gain has been obtained. Moreover, the high-order mode oscillation is suppressed effectively, And an output power of 1.95 GW corresponding to 26% efficiency and 62 dB gain has been obtained in the laboratory.

articleTitle: A novel impedance converter for 2.45G magnetron
abstract: In this paper, a novel hammer-shaped impedance converter structure model for 2.45G magnetron is built in CST. Compared with the traditional impedance converter, it is found that the insertion loss and the reflection coefficient of the novel structure are obviously improved.

articleTitle: First high power results from the 57.12 GHz 5th harmonic frequency multiplier
abstract: Traditional linear interaction RF sources (klystrons and traveling wave tubes) provide limited amounts of power at the mm-wave and terahertz part of the spectrum because their critical dimensions have to be small compared to the wavelength they operate. Due to these small dimensions, the amount of current that can go through the beam apertures is limited. We designed, built and hot-tested a new gyrocon-like mm-wave source, with an output interaction circuit based on a spherical sector cavity. This spherical sector cavity provides a large beam aperture, allowing for a significant amount of current to go through. This source operates as a 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic frequency multiplier, with an output frequency of 57.12 GHz. The measured peak output power was 54.26 W at the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic, while power at the other harmonics was at least 33.28 dB lower than the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic.

articleTitle: Upgrading the 250kW CW X-band klystron used in the goldstone solar system radar
abstract: The Goldstone Solar System Radar (GSSR), part of the Deep Space Network (DSN), utilizes a 70 meter antenna and a 500kW CW transmitter powered by two VKX-7864B, 250kW CW X-band (8560 MHz) klystrons. The VKX-7864B klystron, developed in 1988, required improvements in power output, bandwidth, and reliability to ensure long term system sustainability and to support demands of future DSN/GSSR critical missions. CPI reviewed klystron subassemblies historical failure modes, performed simulations with State-of-the-Art computer codes, and identified improvement opportunities. Improvements in the beam optics, RF circuits gain, bandwidth, and efficiency, collector dissipation, coolant flow, thermal stability, and mechanical reliability were implemented in a high reliability klystron upgrade, designated the VKX-7864C. All performance goals were met or exceeded. Power output > 250kW CW over entire 50 MHz bandwidth, gain > 51dB, efficiency > 45%, RF beam transmission > 99.99%. This paper presents some important improvements of this klystron development.

articleTitle: THz electromagnetic radiation in beam-plasma system under different ions' quantity
abstract: Recent simulation study finds that terahertz (THz) electromagnetic (EM) radiation can be excited in beam-plasma system. In addition, the EM radiation in beam-plasma system under different ions' quantity is also studied, and the calculation results are that the EM radiation frequency under the same plasma ions' quantity is all the same, but under different plasma ions' quantity, the electromagnetic radiation frequencies are different. The related physical explanation is also given in this paper.

articleTitle: Genetic algorithm optimization of collector for W band Gyro-TWT
abstract: The collector is an important component in a Gyro-Travelling Wave Tube. The performance influences the capability of tube. The curved geometry is employed to average the dissipated power distribution. Compared to the previous cylindrical geometry, the maximum dissipated power is reduced from 0.83 kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.396 kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The temperature on inner wall is reduced from 227 °C to 116 °C. The capability of collector is improved. Also the stability analysis is done, and it shows the curved geometry can operate stably.

articleTitle: Analysis of copropagating electron beams interaction in a smooth waveguide
abstract: Linear theory methods of the coupled spacecharge waves for copropagating electron beams considering coefficients of electron interaction and a reduction of plasma oscillations are developed. Interaction of copropagating electron beams promising to amplification of microwaves in electron mode regimes to create devices of millimeter and submillimeter wavelength ranges. Equations of the coupled waves are written down and solutions of the dispersive equation in coupling regime of three and four waves are received. Large signal modes are investigated within model of large particles which has carried out the trajectory analysis of interaction processes of two copropagating electron beams with differ energy. Features of interaction modes with the gain and no gain waves are considered.

articleTitle: Simulation of a sheet beam using a thermionic cathode and a microfabricated anode for a W-band traveling-wave tube
abstract: A sheet beam is simulated using published data of scandia doped dispenser cathode with anti-emission mask structure for a W-band traveling wave tube. The emission properties of the beam are studied with different mask thicknesses, temperatures and anodes. The emission current densities and beam trajectories for these conditions are reported. The required beam cross-section is achieved with an emission current density of ~34 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a cathode emission area of 0.35× 0.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> using a microfabricated anode without needing a beam-forming electrode.

articleTitle: Development of a 358 MHz, 3.1 MW pulsed klystron for proton accelerator
abstract: This work presents some preliminary results of the design of a klystron amplifier to be used as RF power source of a radio-frequency quadrupole for a proton linac accelerator. The main goals of the RF klystron design are: 358 MHz of central frequency, with a bandwidth of ± 2MHz, 3.1 MW of peak power, pulsed length of 1.5 ms, and pulse repetition rate of 50 Hz. A theoretical electronic efficiency of 55% was found when the klystron cathode is driven by voltage pulses of 115 kV and 49 A of beam current.

articleTitle: Study of multibeam relativistic vircator
abstract: We have developed and investigated the multibeam relativistic vircator scheme. The effect of synchronization of virtual cathodes oscillations that is manifested in the “imposition” of the spectral characteristics by the beam with the highest current to the entire system has been discovered. We have done a multiparameter analysis of the multibeam vircator and obtained the maps of the character regimes of system dynamics. The possibility of significant increase of output microwave power in the system with four electron beams in comparison with the single-beam system has been shown.

articleTitle: Design and nano-CNC fabrication of modified sine waveguide for 300 GHz traveling-wave tube
abstract: A sine waveguide is a slow-wave structure proposed recently for terahertz traveling-wave tube. The sine waveguide is known to have better transmission and reflection characteristics compared to slow-wave structures. There are several ways of fabricating terahertz slow-wave structures. A nano-CNC machining is a technique that has a couple of advantages over other methods. For fabrication to be possible, the sine waveguide should be modified. Simulations were conducted to compare the original and modified structures. The results show that S-parameters and dispersion curve are similar. The measurement of S-parameters of fabricated structure was done using a vector network analyzer. The measurement result shows that high transmission loss exists in the measurement result. The transmission loss in the modified sine waveguide will be analyzed in the future.

articleTitle: Perspectives of using autocathodes in high-power microwave devices
abstract: This work presents the results of the analysis of perspective usage of auto emission cathodes in O-type high-power microwave devices - klystrons and TWT. The issues of time stability of characteristics of auto emission cathodes, their influence on electrical strength of devices, some operational characteristics have been studied.

articleTitle: Analytical and numerical simulation of multipactor within a helical resonant filter
abstract: Multipactor analysis of a helical resonant filter has been performed using CST Particle Studio and analytically using a 1-D particle tracking code, based on the Runge-Kutta-Nystrom method. A comparison of results is presented.

articleTitle: Design of a W-band Gyro-TWT with high velocity ratio and low voltage
abstract: The design and simulation of a high velocity ratio, low voltage W band gyro-TWT operating in the fundamental TE01 mode is presented. Two major sections including magnetron electron gun (MIG) and interaction circuit are designed. The MIG achieves velocity ratio (α) of 1.6 and velocity spread (Δβ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>) of 0.91% in the operating frequency band. The interaction in this design consisted of three stages distributed-loss structure. 3D-PIC code and nonlinear self-consistent steady-state code are employed in the design and simulation. The simulation results show that the amplifier can generate a saturated power of 35kW in 93GHz when operate at a 40kV, 2A electron beam with α of 1.6 and Δβ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf> of 3%.

articleTitle: Design and cold simulation of a metal PBG cavity for sub-millimeter wave gyrotron
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of a metal photonic band gap (PBG) cavity is presented for sub-millimeter wave gyrotrons. A triangular unit cell of a regular metal PBG structure has been investigated using an ADI-FDTD numerical algorithm. The dispersion of this unit cell is plotted in order to study the nature of propagation of electromagnetic (EM) wave. The metal PBG cavity is realized by making a defect in the 2-D periodic triangular structure. The designed PBG cavity is modeled in `CST Microwave Studio' for observing the mode purity and its propagation and reflection behaviors. The transient analysis of the cavity predicted its return loss as ~ 32.45 dB and its quality factor as 7830 at 250 GHz.

articleTitle: Long-life photocathodes with high quantum efficiency
abstract: This program is developing high quantum efficiency (QE), reservoir cathodes for accelerators, free-electron lasers, ultra-fast electron microscopes and other applications. High QE materials are deposited on an emitter sealing a reservoir of cesium chromate and titanium powders. An integral heater provides a controlled flow of cesium to replace that lost by evaporation, thereby extending the lifetime of the cathode. Experiments demonstrated these cathodes can recover from poisoning events, including atmospheric contamination. A facility is being developed to fabricate the cathodes and transport them to user facilities.

articleTitle: Corrosion mitigation coatings for RF sources and components
abstract: Research is continuing to develop nanometer-scale, ceramic coatings to reduce or eliminate corrosion in cooling channels of RF sources and components. The coatings separate the metal substrate from the coolant, preventing corrosion and erosion. This is addressing issues in remote or mobile environments where high quality coolant fluids are not available. Previous research demonstrated the effectiveness of alumina and hafnia nanoscale coatings. The current research is investigating additional materials and the optimum thickness and application processes. A prototype application system is being assembled to test with deliverable products. The presentation will describe the latest test results, describe the applications system, and provide the schedule for the program.

articleTitle: RF system for the MICE demonstration of ionisation cooling
abstract: Muon accelerators offer an attractive option for a range of future particle physics experiments. They can enable high energy (TeV+) high energy lepton colliders whilst mitigating the difficulty of synchrotron losses, and can provide intense beams of neutrinos for fundamental physics experiments investigating the physics of flavor. The method of production of muon beams results in high beam emittance which must be reduced for efficient acceleration. Conventional emittance control schemes take too long, given the very short (2.2 microsecond) rest lifetime of the muon. Ionisation cooling offers a much faster approach to reducing particle emittance, and the international MICE collaboration aims to demonstrate this technique for the first time. This paper will present the MICE RF system and its role in the context of the overall experiment.

articleTitle: Study of W-band diamond RF windows for high-average-power TWTs
abstract: We present a simulation study of a pillbox-type RF window for a W-band TWT. The window consists of a polycrystalline diamond disk brazed into a copper waveguide mode converter assembly. We discuss progress on thermal and electromagnetic simulations, with a view toward establishing high-average-power operating limits regarding electric breakdown and thermal overload.

articleTitle: Experiment of 0.34 THz relativistic backward-wave oscillator
abstract: The design of 0.34THz relativistic backward-wave oscillator (RBWO) is presented in this paper. The sine slow-wave structure has been fabricated successfully though technical study. The measurement methods of pulse width, frequency, and power for the nanosecond, high-power, THz signal have been studied. In the experiment the RBWO produced THz radiation with power 600kW, frequency in the range of 0.32THz~0.36THz, pulse width 1.66ns, and it could operate at the pulse repetitive frequency 10Hz.

articleTitle: Measurements of structures for vacuum electronic sources manufactured by 3D printing
abstract: Periodic structures that reduce the velocity of electromagnetic wave propagation are widely used in electron beam driven microwave vacuum electronic sources. When the frequency increases into the mm-wave region such structures become difficult to manufacture because of the small physical dimensions. “Additive Manufacturing” or “3D printing” offers the possibility of constructing certain types of components quickly, efficiently and relatively inexpensively. Many questions arise however, including what structural resolution is obtainable, the surface roughness, surface electrical resistivity and vacuum compatibility. To address some of these questions the performance of a periodic structure manufactured using a 3D printing technique and designed for W-band operation (75-110GHz) is evaluated and reported in the present work.

articleTitle: Design considerations of TWT magnet stacks
abstract: The main important design considerations for the magnet assembly in traveling wave tube (TWT) stacks are: permeance coefficient, pole piece saturation, positions of the input and output coupler magnets and thermal stability of the magnet grades used in the stacks. Careful considerations of the constraints and tradeoffs in the early design stage would maximize the chance of success in the development of new TWT magnet stacks.

articleTitle: Measurement of a W-band output launcher system for a broadband gyro-TWA
abstract: An output system for a W-band (90-100 GHz) gyrotron-traveling wave amplifier is designed, simulated, measured and the results are presented. This is an updated system based on a previous design and the output shows more favorable properties for the amplifiers intended application, as a millimetre wave source in a cloud sensing radar. A greater than -30 dB reflection was measured over the frequency range and high Gaussian content obtained.

articleTitle: Reentrant double-staggered ladder coupled-cavity structure for X-band traveling-wave tube
abstract: The paper describes the design of an X-band coupled-cavity traveling-wave tube (CC-TWT) based on the reentrant double-staggered ladder coupled-cavity slow wave structure (SWS) using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) and particle-in-cell (PIC) code in Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Particle Studio. When the cathode voltage and cathode current are 25.9 kV and 5 A, respectively, the PIC simulation results show that the corresponding saturated output power is over 20kW from 8.6 to 9.7 GHz, the maximum output power can reach 28.8 kW at 9.2 GHz, and the electronic efficiency and the gain can reach over 15.6% and 40 dB.

articleTitle: Design and experiment of 0.13THz folded-waveguide oscillator
abstract: This paper shows the design and experiment results of the 0.13THz folded-waveguide oscillator. The folded-waveguide structure has been manufactured successfully though CNC machining. The initial tube has been fabricated and tested. According the experiment, The initial tube gets the maximum continuous output power about 6W at 0.13THz from a 15.6 kV, 29 mA electron beam. The electric tunable bandwidth is only about 1GHz in the range of 0.129THz ~ 0.13THz, by the reason of the electron-optical system.
